title: Message 90001
text:
Both x and y arguments are required when either is passed to raise, but only \<argument_name\> was provided.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The messaging infrastructure detected a call to the internal raise() function with only one of the required coordinate pair arguments (x or y). Both must be provided together or neither should be provided.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 3018
text:
GPU memory allocation on device \<device_id\> failed with code \<allocator_error_code\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A GPU memory allocation failed on the specified device. The device ID and allocator error code are shown in the message. This typically occurs when the GPU does not have sufficient free memory to run the simulation.


Suggestions
This typically occurs when the GPU does not have sufficient free memory to run the simulation. Reducing the mesh size or the number of active modules may lower memory requirements. If multiple simulations are running on the same GPU, consider running them sequentially or on separate devices.

title: Message 3002
text:
Non-CUDA_SUCCESS code returned (\<cuda_error_code\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The GPU solver returned a non-success CUDA error code. The error code is shown in the message. This typically indicates a CUDA driver or device error that prevented the GPU computation from completing.


Suggestions
Check the CUDA error code for more detail. Common causes include insufficient GPU memory, a driver version mismatch or a hardware fault. Ensure the NVIDIA driver is up to date and that the GPU is functioning correctly. Running nvidia-smi in the terminal can help confirm the device status.

Release Version: 2026.2.0

Ensure the number of particle groups defined in the particle tracking control file matches the run that produced the restart file. If the configuration has changed, a new restart file must be generated.

Description
One or more particles could not be tracked during the current timestep. The number of affected particles is shown in the message. Those particles are removed from tracking and the simulation continues.


Suggestions
If particle loss is unexpected, consider reducing the Lagrangian Timestep == or Eulerian Timestep == commands in the particle tracking control file. Check the model domain extent and wet/dry behaviour in the region where particles are being tracked.

Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No default material block has been defined in the sediment transport control file. Without a default material, every material ID in the mesh must have its properties explicitly specified. If any material is missing a definition, an error will be raised at runtime.


Suggestions
Add a Material == Default block to the sediment transport control file to define default sediment properties. Individual material blocks can then partially overwrite the defaults where needed.

title: Message 11022
text:
Erosion model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An erosion model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Erosion Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected erosion model.

title: Message 11020
text:
Depending on group model selection, d50 parameter may need to be set.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The median grain size (d50) has not been set for this sediment fraction. Depending on the model selections, d50 may be required to correctly compute sediment transport rates.


Suggestions
Add the d50 == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file. If d50 is not required by the selected models this warning can be ignored.

title: Message 11018
text:
Critical stress model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A critical stress model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Critical Stress Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected critical stress model.

title: Message 11016
text:
Bedshear model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The bed shear model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Bed Shear Parameters == command to the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected bed shear model.

title: Message 11014
text:
Bed slumping model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The bed slumping model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Bed Slumping Parameters == command to the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected bed slumping model.

title: Message 11012
text:
"External" model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The external sediment transport model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the External Model Parameters == command to the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected external model.

title: Message 11010
text:
restart file incompatible with sediment control file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of 2d cells stored in the sediment restart file does not match the current mesh. The restart file was generated from a different mesh and cannot be used to initialise the sediment bed state.


Suggestions
Ensure the restart file was produced using the same mesh as the current run. If the mesh has changed, a new restart file must be generated or the bed must be initialised from another source.

title: Message 11008
text:
floating point error returned by settling model at cell\<2d_cell_id\>, layer \<layer_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was returned by the settling velocity model at the reported cell and layer (this is the 2D or 3D layer of the water column, not the sediment bed). This indicates a numerical failure in the settling calculation.


Suggestions
Check the model conditions at the reported cell and layer. Review the Settling Model == and accompanying Settling Parameters == command for the sediment type(s) for unrealistic parameterisation. Review the SETRATE map output parameter for evidence on unusual settling rates. If the configuration appears reasonable, reducing the sediment transport timestep (using the sediment control file Update dt == command) may help resolve the issue.

title: Message 11006
text:
floating point error returned by bedload model at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was returned by the bedload transport model at the reported cell. This indicates a numerical failure in the bedload calculation.


Suggestions
Check the model for extreme or unrealistic sediment flux values near the reported cell. Review the output hydraulic model bed shear stress (TAUB) and sediment transport bed shear stresses (TAUC, TAUW and TAUCW if applicable). The BEDLOAD or BEDLOAD_TOTAL map outputs may assist in assessing spurious bedload rates. Review the specified sediment fraction models for high or unrealistic parameterisation of the Bedload Model == and accompanying Bedload Parameters == command for the sediment type(s).
If the sediment fraction configuration appears reasonable, reducing the sediment transport timestep (using the sediment control file Update dt == command) may help resolve the issue.

title: Message 11004
text:
VanRijn04 external model must be enabled in order to provide variable inputs into VanRijn04 bedrough/bedshear/settling/erosion/bedload model/s



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more sediment transport sub-models (bed roughness, bed shear, settling, erosion or bedload) have been set to vanRijn04 but the external model has not been set to vanRijn04. The external model must be enabled when any of these sub-models use vanRijn04 as it provides the shared variable inputs required across sub-models.


Suggestions
Add External Model == vanRijn04 to the sediment transport control file, or change the affected sub-model selections to a model that does not require the external vanRijn04 module.

title: Message 11002
text:
Maximum allowable bed thickness limit (100.0 m) is exceeded at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total initial bed thickness at the reported cell exceeds the hard limit of 100 m. This is calculated from the initial sediment mass and dry bulk density specified for each bed layer. Layer thickness is derived as mass divided by dry bulk density for each sediment fraction, summed across all fractions and layers.


Suggestions
Review the Initial Mass == and Dry Density == values in the bed layer definition for the reported cell’s material. Check that the values are physically reasonable and that no data entry errors have been made in the sediment transport control file or initial condition inputs.

title: Message 11000
text:
Error processing material group specification.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A material definition references a group index that exceeds the number of material groups defined in the mesh file. The number of material groups is set in the .2dm file and determines the valid range for Material Group ==.


Suggestions
Check the Material Group == value in the sediment transport control file and ensure it does not exceed the number of material groups encoded in the .2dm mesh file.

title: Message 10390
text:
Error reading input file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more errors were encountered while reading the TUFLOW FV Control File (.fvc). TUFLOW FV has stopped after reaching the maximum number of input file errors. The earlier error messages in the log will identify which lines failed to parse.


Suggestions
Review the log file for the input errors reported before this message and correct each one in the .fvc.

title: Message 10388
text:
ZLine Point not snapped to Line - ignoring



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A point in the ZLine GIS input was not associated with any ZLine polyline and has been ignored. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the unsnapped point.


Suggestions
Check that all points in the ZLine GIS file are correctly snapped to a ZLine polyline. Points that are not connected to a line will not be used to modify the mesh bed elevation.

title: Message 10386
text:
No GPU devices found, enabled or compatible



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not find any CUDA-capable GPU devices when initialising the GPU solver. This occurs when GPU mode is enabled (via Hardware == GPU in the control file, or the -pu or -GPU command line arguments) but no compatible NVIDIA GPU is available on the machine, the device is disabled, or the required drivers are not installed.


Suggestions
Verify that a CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU is installed and enabled on the machine. Run nvidia-smi in the terminal or console to confirm the device is detected by the operating system. If nvidia-smi returns no output or an error, the GPU is not visible to the operating system — check that the device is enabled and that the NVIDIA driver is installed. If nvidia-smi returns device information successfully, ensure the NVIDIA driver is up to date.
If no GPU is available, remove the -pu or -GPU command line argument, or set Hardware == CPU in the control file to run using the CPU-based solver.

title: Message 10384
text:
CoordSys line could not be found in "MI Projection" .mif file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not find a CoordSys line in the MapInfo .mif file used to define the GIS projection. The file may be empty, corrupt, or missing the coordinate system definition.


Suggestions
Open the .mif file and verify it contains a valid CoordSys line. Check the projection string matches the TUFLOW FV GIS template layers. If the file is empty or corrupt, regenerate it from a valid source layer.

title: Message 10382
text:
XMDF and NetCDF map outputs are incompatible - please choose either XMDF or NetCDF



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Both XMDF and NetCDF map output types have been specified in the same run. These two output formats cannot be used together.


Suggestions
Remove one of the conflicting map output types from the control file so that only XMDF or NetCDF is specified, not both.

title: Message 10380
text:
\<debug_message\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error was triggered by a Debug Error == or Error == command in the control file. The message text shown is taken directly from the value provided in the control file.


Suggestions
Remove or comment out the Debug Error == or Error == command from the control file if it is no longer needed.

title: Message 10378
text:
"BC Event Source" must include two values separated by "|"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A BC Event Source == entry in the event file does not contain the required | separator. The command expects a variable name and a value separated by a pipe character.


Suggestions
Check the BC Event Source == entries in the event file and ensure each one follows the format BC Event Source == variable_name | value.

title: Message 10376
text:
singular matrix in ludcmp



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A singular matrix was encountered in an internal linear equation solver.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10374
text:
error calculating bilinear interpolation weights



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The bilinear interpolation weights calculated for a triangular cell fell outside the valid range. This can occur with highly distorted or degenerate triangular cells in the mesh.


Suggestions
Review the mesh quality for highly skewed or degenerate triangular cells. Improving mesh quality in affected areas may resolve this error.

title: Message 10372
text:
NSTACK too small



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An internal sorting routine exceeded its pre-allocated stack depth.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10370
text:
argument to -pu option cannot be negative



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The GPU Device ID provided with the -pu command line argument is negative. A valid device ID must be zero or a positive integer.


Suggestions
Correct the -pu argument to use a valid non-negative device ID. Device IDs are zero-based (for example, -pu0 for the first GPU).

title: Message 10368
text:
Missing value after scenario argument: \<scenario_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A -s scenario argument was found on the command line but no scenario value followed it. The scenario key shown in the message was the last argument provided.


Suggestions
Ensure the -s argument is followed by a scenario value. For example: -s scenario_name.

title: Message 10366
text:
User defined second order turbulence parameters group not set.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The second order vertical mixing model has been enabled but no parameter group has been specified. A parameter group is required to define the turbulence closure coefficients.


Suggestions
Add the Second Order Vertical Mixing Model Parameter Group == command and set it to a supported group. Refer to the TUFLOW FV documentation for available options.

title: Message 10364
text:
NaN returned from internal turbulence module



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The turbulence module returned a NaN (not-a-number) value for the eddy viscosity or diffusivity. This indicates an instability within the vertical turbulence closure scheme during the simulation.


Suggestions
Review the turbulence model settings and check the model for numerically extreme conditions such as very large velocities or sharp gradients.

title: Message 10362
text:
Could not make directory: \<tpc_directory\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV attempted to create the output directory shown in the message but the operation failed. This typically indicates a file system permissions issue or an invalid path.


Suggestions
Check that TUFLOW FV has permission to write to the output location and that the parent output directory is accessible. If running on a Linux Operating System, ensure the user has write permissions for the parent output folder.

title: Message 10360
text:
\<sample_parameter\> not included in simulation.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The parameter specified by Sample Parameter == for this structure’s control logic is not active in the simulation. For example, salinity or temperature may not be enabled, or the referenced sediment, tracer, or water quality constiuents may exceed the number of classes configured for the run.


Suggestions
Check that the module or class referenced by Sample Parameter == is enabled and configured in the simulation. If the parameter is not needed for control, update Sample Parameter == to a parameter that is active in the run.

title: Message 10358
text:
downstream water levels for structure matrix not in ascending order



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The downstream water level values in the structure matrix file are not in ascending order. TUFLOW FV requires these values to be sorted from lowest to highest.


Suggestions
Open the matrix file specified by the Flux File == command for this structure and sort the downstream water level values in ascending order.

title: Message 10356
text:
Zone ID, \<zone_id\>has fewer than 3 vertices.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The GIS zone polygon identified by the reported zone ID has fewer than 3 vertices. A valid polygon requires at least 3 vertices to define an enclosed area.


Suggestions
Open the GIS layer containing this zone and inspect the polygon for the reported zone ID. Correct the geometry so that it forms a valid closed polygon with at least 3 vertices. Check that no duplicate vertices exist. If ensure, delete and re-digitise the polygon.

title: Message 10354
text:
Weir elevation property has not been set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The weir crest elevation has not been set for this structure. Flux Function == Weir requires an absolute weir crest elevation to be specified via the Properties == command. This value cannot be omitted or defaulted.


Suggestions
Provide the weir crest elevation via the Properties == command for this structure.
If a crest elevation relative to the bed is preferred, switch the Flux Function == to Weir_dz instead. These flux types accept a delta-Z offset and will default to zero if the elevation property is not supplied.

title: Message 10352
text:
Wall flux function is not applicable to linked nodestring or linked zone structures.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Flux Function == Wall is only supported for single nodestring structures. It cannot be used with linked nodestring or linked zone structure types.


Suggestions
Change the Flux Function == to a supported type for this structure, or change the structure type to a single nodestring if a wall boundary is required.

title: Message 10350
text:
Unrecognised structure type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unexpected internal state. The structure type was not recognised during structure initialisation.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10348
text:
Unrecognised structural control specification



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The control type specified using Control == is not recognised or is not supported in this context.


Suggestions
Correct the value in Control == structure sub-block to a supported type.

title: Message 10346
text:
Unrecognised destratification unit type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The destratification unit type specified using Destratification Unit == is not recognised.


Suggestions
Correct the value in Destratification Unit == structure block to a supported type.

title: Message 10344
text:
Unexpected structure nodestring id, \<nodestring_id\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
During structure initialisation, TUFLOW FV could not find a nodestring matching the ID specified in the structure block definition. Each hydraulic structure that uses a nodestring connection must reference a nodestring ID that is present in the mesh or input GIS nodestring layers.


Suggestions
Check that the nodestring ID reported in the message matches an ID in the 2d_ns GIS layer used by the model or in the .2dm file (in the .2dm search for lines starting with NS). Common causes are a typographical error in the structure definition file, or the nodestring GIS layer not being read by the model.
Confirm that the Read GIS Nodestring command for the nodestring layer is present in the control file and that the file path is correct.

title: Message 10342
text:
TIME column must be monotonically increasing



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Time column in a structure csv file is not monotonically increasing. This column must be sorted in ascending order. This can occur in files specified by Control File == or Target File ==.


Suggestions
Review the csv Time column for duplicate entries or non-ascending order and rerun the model.

title: Message 10340
text:
Structure max open width MUST be defined for linked zone structure type.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Linked zone structures require a maximum open width to be specified. This value is used to to complete hydraulic stability checks and is required to be manually specified for linked zone structure connections. This applies to structure blocks with Flux Function == options where the structure width cannot be inferred from the flux function geometry.
```


Suggestions
Add the Max Open Width == command to the linked zone structure block. This value should represent the maximum width of the structure opening when fully open.

title: Message 10338
text:
Structure control parameter is not recognised: \<control_parameter\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The control parameter named in the message is not a recognised value.


Suggestions
Correct the value in Control Parameter == command to one of the supported options.

title: Message 10336
text:
Structure control logic is not defined, set to type NONE



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A structure control logic type was not defined for one or more control parameters. TUFLOW FV has defaulted to none (overwrite) logic for these parameters.


Suggestions
To suppress this warning, explicitly set the logic type using Control Logic == in the structure control block for each entry in the accompanying Control Parameters == command.

title: Message 10334
text:
Sampling time has not been set for structure control



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A sampling interval is required for this structure control but has not been set.


Suggestions
Add Sample dt == to the structure control block to specify the sampling interval (in hours). For example Sample dt == 0.25 will sample the model Sample Parameter every 15 minutes.

title: Message 10332
text:
SAMPLE_VALUE column must be monotonically increasing



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Sample_Value column in the csv specified by the Control File == command is not monotonically increasing. This column must be sorted in ascending order for the rule lookup to work correctly.


Suggestions
Review the control file csv Sample_Value column for duplicate entries or non-ascending order and reun the model

title: Message 10330
text:
Porous structure hydraulic conductivity has not been specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The hydraulic conductivity required for the porous structure flux calculation has not been set.


Suggestions
Add the hydraulic conductivity to the Properties == command for this structure.

title: Message 10328
text:
Only a single cell is supported for bubbler destratification unit: \<2d_cell_count\> cells were assigned



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A bubbler destratification unit must be placed in a zone polygon that contains exactly one 2D cell centroid. The zone polygon assigned to this structure captured more than one cell.


Suggestions
Resize or reposition the zone polygon so that it contains only a single 2D cell centroid. The number of cells found is shown in the message.

title: Message 10326
text:
Number of control headers exceeds the number of control parameters.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of column headers specified using Control Header == exceeds the number of control parameters specified using Control Parameter ==. Each header must correspond to a control parameter.


Suggestions
Check that Control Header == and Control Parameter == specify the same number of entries. Remove any extra headers, or add the corresponding control parameters.

title: Message 10324
text:
No zone corresponding to ID, \<zone_id\>, found in any GIS ZN file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not find a zone with the specified ID. The zone ID named in the message does not match any polygon IDs supplied by 2d_zn layers and Read GIS Zone == commands.


Suggestions
Check that the zone ID(s) requested in the Structure == command matches a 2d_zn polygon name specified by the Read GIS Zone == command.

title: Message 10322
text:
NS or ZN component must be constructed prior to FLUX component



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unexpected internal state during structure initialisation. The nodestring or zone component was not available at the point it was required.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10320
text:
Flux function must be specified for linked zone structures. The default NLSWE flux function is not applicable.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Linked zone structure connection types require a Flux Function == to be specified. The default Flux Function == NLSWE cannot be used.


Suggestions
Set the structure block Flux Function == command to a valid flux function for the linked zone structure connection type.

title: Message 10318
text:
Error processing sampling coordinates for structure



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sample point coordinates (specified using the Sample Point == control block command) for a structure control are missing or invalid. Valid X and Y coordinates must be provided when using a point or profile sample type for structure control.


Suggestions
Check that a valid sample point is specified in the structure control block and that the coordinates are within the model domain.

title: Message 10316
text:
Duplicated control parameter is detected: \<control_parameter\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The same control parameter was specified more than once for a structure control. The parameter named in the message appears at least twice in the Control Parameter == configuration.


Suggestions
Remove the duplicate entry from Control Parameter ==, keeping only one instance of each parameter.

title: Message 10314
text:
Crest elevation property has not been set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The crest elevation property for a wave pump structure has not been set. This property is required for the wave pump structure type.


Suggestions
Set the crest elevation property in the wave pump structure configuration.

title: Message 10312
text:
Control type SAMPLE_RULE does not support multiple controls yet.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sample rule structure control type Control == Sample_Rule was configured with more than one control parameter. Only one control parameter is currently supported with the sample rule control type.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of Control Parameter == input values to one, rather than a comma delimited list or multiple values.

title: Message 10310
text:
Compression properties have not been correctly specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more properties of the destratification unit have been set to a negative value. All bubbler properties (apart from the pipe elevation) must be non-negative.


Suggestions
Check the destratification unit properties and ensure required inputs values are zero or positive (apart from the pipe elevation).

title: Message 10308
text:
Bubbler properties have not been correctly specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more properties of the destratification unit have been set to a negative value. All bubbler properties (apart from the pipe elevation) must be non-negative.


Suggestions
Check the destratification unit properties and ensure required inputs values are zero or positive (apart from the pipe elevation).

title: Message 10306
text:
Bubbler destratification unit requires the selected 2D cell (\<2d_cell_id\>) to have more than one layer.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The cell containing the destratification unit with the bubbler airflow option has only one vertical layer. Destratification unit structure types require the cell to have more than one vertical layer to simulate mixing across the water column.


Suggestions
Check the bathymetry and layering configuration at the destratification unit location. The cell identified in the message must resolve more than one vertical layer for the unit to operate.

title: Message 10304
text:
Assigned air flow rate property is set to \<variable_name\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The air flow rate property for the destratification unit has been set to a very small or zero value (in m³/s/plume), as shown in the message. The destratification unit may not function as intended with this value.


Suggestions
Check the air flow rate property and set it to the intended positive value.

title: Message 10302
text:
Airflow_Bubbler control parameter must be used for bubbler destratification unit



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A destratification unit structure using the bubbler airflow option and operational control block was configured with a control parameter other than Airflow_Bubbler.


Suggestions
Change the control parameter for the bubbler destratification structure to Airflow_Bubbler.

title: Message 10300
text:
Scenario name is blank. Line Number: \<line_number\> - "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Model Scenarios == line was found with no scenario value on the right hand side.


Suggestions
Add at least one scenario value after Model Scenarios ==, or remove the line if scenarios are not required.

title: Message 10298
text:
Require at least \<min_required_scenarios\> scenarios to be specified to fill \<scenario_wildcard\> placeholders in FVC name



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The control file name contains a scenario or event placeholder with a number higher than the number of values provided. For example, if the name contains ~s3~ but only two scenario values have been specified, this error is raised.


Suggestions
Provide the required number of scenario or event values, or update the control file name so that no placeholder references a position beyond the number of values supplied.

title: Message 10296
text:
Missing scenario value for S\<scenario_number\>. Maximum scenario number: S\<total_scenarios\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A value is missing for the scenario number shown in the message. Scenario numbers must be assigned sequentially. If a higher scenario number is provided, all lower scenario numbers must also have values assigned.


Suggestions
Provide a value for the missing scenario number or reduce the maximum scenario number used so that no gaps exist in the sequence.

title: Message 10294
text:
Missing a "~" after scenario placeholder in FVC name



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A scenario placeholder in the control file name is malformed. A closing ~ is missing. Scenario placeholders must follow the format ~s1~, ~s2~, etc. with both an opening and closing ~.


Suggestions
Check the control file name for scenario placeholders and ensure each one has a matching closing ~.

title: Message 10292
text:
Exceeded allowed maximum number of scenario groups (\<max_scenarios\>). Line Number: \<line_number\> - "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of scenario values specified by the Model Scenarios command exceeds the maximum allowed (<max_scenarios>).


Suggestions
Reduce the number of scenario values to within the allowed maximum shown in the message.

title: Message 10290
text:
\<error_message\> on line \<line_number\> - "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A variable substitution error occurred while processing the line shown in the message. This typically occurs when a variable referenced on the line has not been defined or could not be resolved.


Suggestions
Check the control file and verify that all variables referenced (such as scenario ~s~ or event ~e~ tokens or user defined Set Variable names) are defined before they are used.

title: Message 10288
text:
Unbalanced "DEFINE EVENT"/"END DEFINE" count. Line no: \<line_number\> : "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Define Event block was opened without a matching End Define, or an End Define was found without a preceding Define Event. Every Define Event in the Event File must be closed with a corresponding End Define.


Suggestions
Check the Event File for a missing End Define at or before the line shown, or a End Define that has no matching Define Event.

title: Message 10286
text:
Cannot use "\<log_directory\>" after an "ELSE" statement. Line no: \<line_number\> : "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An Else If Scenario, Else If Event or Else keyword was found on the line shown after an Else block has already been opened. An Else block must be the final branch in a conditional block.


Suggestions
Move any remaining conditions after the Else block. The log file should indicate the offending lines.

title: Message 10284
text:
Cannot start IF block with "\<logic_statement\>". Line no: \<line_number\> : "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An Else, Else If Scenario or Else If Event keyword was encountered on the line shown in the message without a preceding If Scenario or If Event block. These keywords are only valid inside an If/End If conditional block.


Suggestions
Check the control file for a missing If Scenario or If Event before the line shown, or remove the orphaned keyword if it is not needed.

title: Message 10282
text:
\<data_variable\> variable not found in netcdf file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A variable expected in the transport netCDF file was not found. This can occur when the current simulation includes hydrodynamic conditions that were not present in the simulation that generated the transport file, meaning the required variables were never written to it.


Suggestions
Ensure the simulation reading the transport file does not include any hydrodynamic conditions that were not present in the simulation that generated the transport file. If any hydrodynamic conditions or changes to horizontal and vertical turbulence and scalar mixing were added to the simulation after the transport file was generated, a new transport file must be generated that includes all hydrodynamic conditions.

title: Message 10280
text:
\<column_name\> column not found in csv file. Assigning a value of: \<default_value\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A column name expected by TUFLOW FV was not found in the csv file being read. The column is optional and the simulation will continue using the default value shown in the message. This warning may indicate that the column header in the file does not exactly match the name TUFLOW FV expects.


Suggestions
Check that the column header in the csv file matches the name shown in the warning. Column names are not case sensitive but must otherwise be an exact match. If the column is intentionally omitted and the default value shown is appropriate for the model then the warning can be ignored. If the default value is not appropriate then add the missing column to the csv file.
For models that include advection dispersion (temperature, salinity or tracers), sediment transport or water quality a default value of NaN typically means the model will use internal model concentrations at the boundary condition location. This can be desirable for flow extractions from the model, or in areas where the boundary condition concentration can be inferred from adjacent model conditions.
It is common for users to specify a ‘dummy’ BC Header to ensure that the BC Default value of a given header entry is used.

title: Message 10278
text:
unexpected format request



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised format was requested when echoing mesh geometry data. The supported formats are ASCII and NETCDF. This is an unexpected condition that should not occur under normal operation.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the simulation log file. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10276
text:
netcdf file variables and grid dimensions are not compatible



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The grid dimensions defined for the boundary condition do not match the variable dimensions found in the netCDF file. The number of grid points in X (NI) and Y (NJ) in the grid specification must match the corresponding dimensions of the data variables in the netCDF file.


Suggestions
Check that the grid specification dimensions match the dimensions of the variables in the netCDF boundary condition file. Use a tool such as the TUFLOW FV Python Toolbox or TUFLOW FV MATLAB Toolbox to inspect the variable dimensions in the file.

title: Message 10274
text:
Unable to find coordinate variable name in netcdf file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more of the coordinate variable names (X, Y or Z) configured for a grid netCDF boundary condition file could not be found in that file. The coordinate variable names must match variables that exist in the netCDF file.


Suggestions
Check the coordinate variable names specified for the grid boundary condition and confirm they match the actual variable names in the netCDF file. Use a tool such as the TUFLOW FV Python Toolbox or TUFLOW FV MATLAB Toolbox to inspect the variable names in the file.

title: Message 10272
text:
Output dataset is not compatible with SMS dat file type.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A multi-dimensional dataset (rank >= 3) was requested for an SMS DAT output block. The SMS DAT format only supports scalar (rank = 1) and 2D vector (rank = 2) datasets.


Suggestions
Select the netCDF output type for the affected output parameter, or remove the incompatible output parameter from the SMS DAT output block.

title: Message 10270
text:
No variable name specified on line \<line_number\> - "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Set Variable  == command was found on the line shown in the message without a variable name. The Set Variable  == command requires both a variable name and a value to be specified.


Suggestions
Update the line to use the format Set Variable  == . For example, Set Variable MY_VARIABLE == 1.0 would set the variable named MY_VARIABLE to the value 1.0.

title: Message 10268
text:
Expecting to find OGCM bc specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Initial Condition OGCM is being applied but no OBC_GRID boundary condition is found in the model. An OBC_GRID boundary condition must be defined when using OGCM initial conditions.


Suggestions
Add an OBC_GRID boundary condition to the model, or remove or comment out the OGCM initial condition if OGCM forcing is not intended.

title: Message 10266
text:
unknown parameter type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An output parameter was specified that is not supported for the output type being written.


Suggestions
Check the output block and remove or replace the unsupported parameter.

title: Message 10264
text:
XMDF output is not supported in this build.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An XMDF output block was specified, but this build of TUFLOW FV was not compiled with XMDF support. XMDF output is only available in builds that include the XMDF library.


Suggestions
Use a different output format such as netCDF, or obtain a TUFLOW FV build that includes XMDF support.

title: Message 10262
text:
Unrecognised output type to convert units: \<output_type\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An internal output type was passed to the unit conversion routine that is not recognised. This is an unexpected condition or unsupported output configuration.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the simulation log file. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10260
text:
Unknown output parameter type '\<output_parameter\>' encountered in output request \<output_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised output parameter type was specified in an output block in the control file. The parameter name and the output block number are reported. TUFLOW FV supports a defined set of output parameter names and does not recognise the value shown.


Suggestions
Check the Output Parameters == command in the output block shown in the message for typographical errors. Parameter names are not case sensitive.

title: Message 10258
text:
Statistics not supported for mass balance outputs. Exiting.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A statistics output interval has been configured for a mass balance output block. Statistics (such as minimum, maximum or time-averaged values) are not supported for mass balance outputs.


Suggestions
Remove the statistics configuration from the MassBalance output block.

title: Message 10256
text:
Output point \<point_label\> is outside model domain.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An output point is located outside the active model domain. No data will be recorded for this output point during the simulation.


Suggestions
Check the coordinates of the output point against the model domain extent. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the point which can be used to confirm whether it is correctly positioned.

title: Message 10254
text:
Output parameter '\<output_parameter\>' is not supported by the SMS DAT format.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The output parameter named in the message is not supported by the SMS DAT (.dat) format.


Suggestions
Change the output format for the output parameter to netCDF, or remove the parameter from the SMS DAT output block.

title: Message 10252
text:
Multiple mass balance output blocks specified. Exiting.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
More than one MassBalance output block has been specified in the control file. Only one mass balance output block is permitted per simulation.


Suggestions
Check the control file for duplicate MassBalance output blocks and remove all but one.

title: Message 10250
text:
Error processing output curtain object. NaN detected in curtain coordinates.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when constructing a curtain output object and NaN values are detected in the interpolated curtain coordinates. This indicates an internal mapping error between the curtain polyline and the mesh.


Suggestions
Check that the curtain polyline file specified via Output Curtain File == is valid and lies fully within the model domain. If the polyline is correct, contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the TUFLOW FV log file and the curtain polyline file, this will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10248
text:
Error echoing spatial output log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing to the spatial output log file (_geo_out.csv) fails. This file records the mapping between output points and their corresponding mesh cell locations and is written to the log directory.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the log directory and that the directory remains writable during the simulation.

title: Message 10246
text:
DAT file output does not support \<output_parameter\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
SMS binary DAT file output does not support water quality list parameters such as WQ_ALL, WQ_LIST, WQ_DIAG_ALL or WQ_DIAG_LIST. These parameters expand to multiple variables and are not supported in the DAT format.


Suggestions
Replace the list parameter with individual water quality variable names in the DAT output block, or use a netCDF output format which supports list parameters.

title: Message 10244
text:
3d output is not supported by csv points file. Requested output will be 2D depth-averaged.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a 3D output parameter is requested with CSV points output format. The CSV points format only supports 2D depth averaged data. The output will be written as a depth averaged result instead.


Suggestions
If 3D layer output at specific points is required, use the Profile output type. If depth averaged output is acceptable, no action is required.

title: Message 10242
text:
Very small edge length encountered at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A very short cell edge was detected during mesh preprocessing. This typically indicates near duplicate nodes or a poorly formed element in the mesh and can affect numerical accuracy, stability and speed during the simulation.


Suggestions
Review the mesh near the flagged cell. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the short edge and can be used to identify the problem area. Check for duplicate or near duplicate nodes and regenerate the mesh with improved element quality.

title: Message 10240
text:
Very large angle encountered at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A very large interior angle was detected at a cell vertex during mesh preprocessing. Cells with interior angles approaching 180° have nearly collinear consecutive vertices and indicate poor mesh quality. This can affect numerical accuracy, stability and speed during the simulation.


Suggestions
Review the mesh in the vicinity of the flagged cell. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the problematic vertex which can be used to identify the area requiring attention. Regenerate the mesh with improved element quality.

title: Message 10238
text:
This does not appear to be a tutorial model. Set "tutorial model == off" to run this simulation (will require a valid license).



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The model control file specifies Tutorial Model == ON (or Demo Model == ON) but the model does not conform to a registered TUFLOW FV tutorial model domain or within the acceptable constraints for demo mode.


Suggestions
If this is a user defined model set Tutorial Model == OFF or Demo Model == OFF in the fvc file. A valid TUFLOW FV license will be required to run the simulation. If this is intended to be a tutorial model verify that the mesh has not been modified from its original form and that the topography and bathymetry does not exceed the original model limits.
For demo mode the model must have fewer than 5000 cells and must not use a restart file or transport file.

title: Message 10236
text:
SMS Licensing has not been enabled in this executable version.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a license cannot be accessed during model license checks. A licence dongle may not be present, the dongle may not hold the required product code, the licence may have expired or there are no available licences. If using a network licence, the licence server may not be accessible or correctly configured.


Suggestions
Refer to the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for further information on licensing and dongle requirements. If the issue persists, Generate a CM Dust File and send both the CM Dust file and TUFLOW FV log file through to support@tuflow.com. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10234
text:
Requested module license not found on available dongle/s.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a license cannot be accessed during model license checks. A licence dongle may not be present, the dongle may not hold the required product code, the licence may have expired or there are no available licences. If using a network licence, the licence server may not be accessible or correctly configured.


Suggestions
Refer to the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for further information on licensing and dongle requirements. If the issue persists, Generate a CM Dust File and send both the CM Dust file and TUFLOW FV log file through to support@tuflow.com. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10232
text:
Could not find suitable licensed dongle/s.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a license cannot be accessed during model license checks. A licence dongle may not be present, the dongle may not hold the required product code, the licence may have expired or there are no available licences. If using a network licence, the licence server may not be accessible or correctly configured.


Suggestions
Refer to the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for further information on licensing and dongle requirements. If the issue persists, Generate a CM Dust File and send both the CM Dust file and TUFLOW FV log file through to support@tuflow.com. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10230
text:
restart file incompatible with geometry file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the cell count stored in a restart file does not match the current mesh. This means the restart file was generated from a different geometry and cannot be used with the current model.


Suggestions
Ensure the restart file corresponds to the same mesh as the current simulation. If the mesh has been modified, the existing restart file cannot be used and the simulation must be started from initial conditions or the restart file must be regenerated from a simulation using the current mesh.

title: Message 10228
text:
file reading error



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when reading the header of an .asc or .flt grid file fails. This occurs when a required header field is missing (NCOLS, NROWS, XLLCENTER/XLLCORNER, YLLCENTER/YLLCORNER, or CELLSIZE).


Suggestions
Open the file and check that all required header fields are present and correctly formatted. For .flt files check the accompanying .hdr file.

title: Message 10226
text:
error writing to log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing to the log file fails during the simulation.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the log directory and that the log file has not been deleted or made read only while the simulation is running.

title: Message 10224
text:
error writing node debug info



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing node debug output to a binary debug snapshot file fails. Node debug output is used occasionally by the TUFLOW FV development team to diagnose issues and is not intended for general use. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
If you see this error contact support@tuflow.com for further assistance.

title: Message 10222
text:
error writing debug file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing a binary debug snapshot file (.dbg) fails. Debug files are used occasionally by the TUFLOW FV development team to diagnose issues and are not intended for general use. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
If you see this error contact support@tuflow.com for further assistance.

title: Message 10220
text:
error writing cell debug info



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing cell debug output fails. It is used occasionly by the TUFLOW FV development team to diagnose issues and is not intended for general use. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
If you see this error contact support@tuflow.com for further assistance.

title: Message 10218
text:
error reading csv file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A csv input file could not be read. This error is raised when a data row cannot be parsed or when a time value in the file is not in a recognised format. It can occur with boundary condition files and other csv inputs read during model initialisation.


Suggestions
Check the csv file identified by the routine shown in the error stack. Open the file and look for rows that contain unexpected content, such as non-numeric values in numeric columns, empty rows or corrupted data.
If the file contains a time column, verify that time values use a consistent and recognised format. The expected time format is dd/mm/yyyy HH:MM:SS or a valid truncation of it.

title: Message 10216
text:
error opening log file, \<log_file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the log file cannot be opened for writing at the start of the simulation. The log file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the log directory exists and is writable. If Log Dir == has been specified, verify the path is correct. On Linux, ensure the user running the simulation has write permission to the log directory.

title: Message 10214
text:
XMDF write error



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing data to an XMDF output file fails during the simulation.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the output directory and that the directory remains writable during the simulation.
If HDF5 file locking is disabled this error can occur when another process is accessing the same XMDF file. Ensure that no other processes are accessing the XMDF file during the simulation unless they also have HDF5 file locking disabled. Contact support@tuflow.com for further information on HDF5 file locking.

title: Message 10212
text:
Unable to open file: \<file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV was unable to open the file shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the file exists at the path shown in the message. Verify that the file path and name are correctly specified in the relevant model control file, including the correct file extension. File paths may be absolute or relative to the location of the model control file.
On Windows ensure the file is not open in another application as this may prevent TUFLOW FV from accessing it. Windows file paths are case insensitve. On Linux file names are case sensitive so ensure the file name and path exactly match the case of the file on disk.

title: Message 10210
text:
Restart file configuration mismatch



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the number of conserved variables stored in the turbulence restart file (_turb.rst) does not match the current model configuration. The model will continue, using restart data for the variables that do match.


Suggestions
This warning typically occurs when a turbulence restart file is applied to a model with a different set of active scalars (e.g. salinity, temperature, tracers) than the run that produced it. Verify that the restart file corresponds to the correct model configuration. If the mismatch is intentional, no action is required.

title: Message 10208
text:
Error writing restart file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing a binary restart file fails. This is applicable to the hydrodynamic (.rst), turbulence (_turb.rst), sediment (_bed.rst) and particle tracking restart files (_ptm.rst).


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the output directory and that the directory remains writable during the simulation. Also check that Write Restart dt is set appropriatelyto avoid writing large restart files too often.

title: Message 10206
text:
Error reading line \<line_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when reading a mesh partition file (specified via Partition File ==) and a line cannot be parsed as a valid integer. The partition file must contain one integer cell partition ID per line. The line number where the error occurred is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the partition file is correctly formatted with one integer value per line and no extraneous content. The file should have been generated by a mesh partitioning tool, regenerate it if it appears corrupt.

title: Message 10204
text:
Error invoking \<netcdf_command\>. Netcdf status value is \<netcdf_status_code\>. \<netcdf_error_message\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A netCDF library call returned an error during model initialisation or runtime. The netCDF command that failed and the error description are shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the netCDF command and error description. The command name indicates the operation that failed. For example nf90_open indicates a file could not be opened and nf90_create indicates an output file could not be created.
If the status code shown is positive it is a system level error number (errno). If it is negative it is a netCDF specific error code. Common causes include an incorrect file path, a file that is not a valid netCDF file, insufficient disk space when writing output and file permission issues.
For system errno values refer to the POSIX errno reference (Linux) or the Windows CRT errno constants (Windows). For netCDF specific error codes refer to the netCDF-C error documentation.

title: Message 10202
text:
Error closing file: \<file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when closing an XMDF output file fails. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
This is typically caused by a file system issue such as insufficient disk space or loss of write access during the simulation. Check available disk space and ensure the output directory remains accessible.

title: Message 10200
text:
Could not create directory: \<directory\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV attempts to create output or check directories during initialisation or file operations. This error occurs when the directory creation attempt fails, typically due to file system permissions or invalid path components.


Suggestions
The parent directory should exist and have write access. On Linux, the user running the model should have write permissions to the parent directory. The specified directory path should be reviewed for invalid characters or excessively long path segments. If a file or other entity with that name already exists in the parent directory, it should be renamed or removed so the directory can be created.

title: Message 10198
text:
NaN detected in global tracer concentration initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the global tracer concentration initial condition value (specified via Initial Tracer Concentration ==) is NaN when applied. This can occur if the value in the control file could not be parsed as a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the Initial Tracer Concentration == line in the control file and ensure a valid numeric value is specified for each tracer being simulated.

title: Message 10196
text:
NaN detected in global sediment concentration initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the global sediment concentration initial condition value (specified via Initial Sediment Concentration ==) is NaN when applied. This can occur if the value in the control file could not be parsed as a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the Initial Sediment Concentration == line in the control file and ensure valid numeric values are specified fro each sediment fraction.

title: Message 10194
text:
NaN detected in global salinity initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the global salinity initial condition value (specified via Initial Salinity ==) is NaN when applied. This can occur if the value in the control file could not be parsed as a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the Initial Salinity == line in the control file and ensure a valid numeric value is specified.

title: Message 10192
text:
Incorrect cell ID specified, \<2d_cell_id\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a cell ID read from a csv initial conditions file is outside the valid range. For Initial Condition 2D == the ID column must contain a valid 2D cell ID. For Initial Condition 3D == it must contain a valid 3D cell ID. The invalid ID is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Open the csv initial conditions file and check the ID column for values that are less than 1 or greater than the number of cells in the mesh. Correct or remove the invalid rows.

title: Message 10190
text:
\<node_count\> unused .2dm nodes found - remove disjoint nodes in mesh.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more nodes in the .2dm mesh file are not connected to any element. The GIS messages output file shows the location of each disjoint node.


Suggestions
Open the mesh in the mesh editor and remove the disjoint nodes. Export the corrected .2dm file before running the simulation again.

title: Message 10188
text:
Partial grid coverage: \<2d_cell_count\> model cells (\<perc_total_2d_cells\> %) fall within grid extent.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Not all model domain mesh cells fall within the extent of the input grid. Cells outside the grid extent will not receive data from this grid source.


Suggestions
Check that the grid extent covers the full model domain. If partial coverage is intentional no action is required. If the coverage gap is unexpected check that the grid file projection and extent match the model domain.

title: Message 10186
text:
unexpected grid type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when an inline grid definition (via Grid Definition ==) specifies an unexpected argument list. This is an internal error and should not occur in normal operation.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the log file. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10184
text:
Specified grid is not coincident with model mesh.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a grid defined via Grid Definition == or Grid Definition File == has no overlap with the model mesh — zero mesh cells or nodes fall within the grid extent. The grid to mesh mapping cannot be constructed.


Suggestions
Check that the grid coordinates and the model mesh are in the same coordinate system and that the grid extents cover the intended area. If the grid is specified inline via Grid Definition ==, verify the origin (x0, y0), rotation angle, cell counts (mx, my), and cell sizes (dx, dy). If specified via a netCDF file using Grid Definition File ==, verify the coordinate variables in that file.

title: Message 10182
text:
NaN detected in grid vertical coordinates



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised after reading the z coordinate variable from a netCDF grid file when one or more values are NaN. This indicates the vertical coordinate data in the file is corrupt or incomplete.


Suggestions
Check the netCDF grid file for missing or invalid values in the z coordinate variable. Re-export or reprocess the file to ensure all vertical coordinate values are finite.

title: Message 10180
text:
Error processing netcdf grid coordinate variables



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the x and y coordinate variables read from a netCDF grid file have an unexpected number of dimensions. TUFLOW FV supports coordinate variables that are either both 1-dimensional (axis-aligned grids) or both 2-dimensional (curvilinear grids); any other combination cannot be processed.


Suggestions
Check that the netCDF grid file is valid and that the variable names specified for the x and y coordinates (via Grid Coordinate Variable Names ==) resolve to variables with either 1 or 2 dimensions each. Re-export or reprocess the grid file if the coordinate variables are malformed.

title: Message 10178
text:
More than the maximum number of scalar constituents (\<max_scalar_constituents\>) have been requested.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total number of scalar constituents (salinity, temperature, suspended sediment fractions, tracers and water quality variables combined) exceeds the internal limit of 100.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of scalar constituents configured. This can be achieved by adjusting one or more of the following.

Disabling salinity and/or temperature if they are not required for the simulation via the Include Salinity == and/or Include Temperature == commands
The number of tracers is controlled by the Ntracer command
The number of suspended sediment fractions specified in the Sediment Control File via the sediment fraction block, bounded by the Fraction and End Fraction commands. Refer to the TUFLOW FV Sediment and Particle Tracking User Manual for more information
The number of water quality variables specified in the Water Quality Control File. Refer to the TUFLOW FV Water Quality User Manual for more information

title: Message 10176
text:
Exceeded maximum number of allowed active BC event sources (\<max_user_variables\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of BC Event Source == variables defined across all Define Event blocks exceeds the internal limit of 100.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of BC event source variables defined.

title: Message 10174
text:
Unnamed polygon/point found in GIS SA layer:\<2d_sa_layer\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A polygon or point in the GIS SA layer has no ID. All features in a GIS SA layer must have an ID to be matched to a boundary condition.


Suggestions
Open the named GIS layer and assign an ID to the unnamed feature. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the unnamed feature.

title: Message 10172
text:
Please use command: 'MATERIAL POLYGON FILE == for CSV file formats. File: \<material_csv\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A csv file was specified for a GIS materials layer input, but csv files are not supported for that command. The Read GIS Mat == command only accepts shp or mif GIS layers.


Suggestions
Use Material Polygon File == instead to specify a csv file for material polygon assignment.
The use of csv inputs for material assignment is deprecated. It is recommended to use GIS integration using 2d_mat GIS inputs and the Read GIS Mat == command.

title: Message 10170
text:
Object in materials polygon is not a region, skipping.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An object in the 2d_mat GIS materials layer has an unrecognised or unsupported geometry type that cannot be read. The object is skipped. The layer expects only polygon (region) objects.


Suggestions
Open the 2d_mat GIS layer and check for objects with unsupported geometry types such as null shapes, lines, text, or multipoint objects. Remove them and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10168
text:
Object in GIS polygon is not a point, skipping.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An object in the 3d_po GIS layer has an unrecognised or unsupported geometry type that cannot be read. The object is skipped.


Suggestions
Open the 3d_po GIS layer and check for objects with unsupported geometry types such as text or multipoint objects. Remove them and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10166
text:
Material ID \<material_id\> using SET MAT == not specified in control file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The material ID specified by Set Mat == has not been defined in the control file’s material blocks. The material ID must be defined before it can be applied globally with Set Mat ==.


Suggestions
Add a material block defining the reported material ID, or change the Set Mat == value to a material ID that is already defined.

title: Message 10164
text:
Inactive material block specification, ID \<material_id\> is not supported with external GIS material layers.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A material ID defined as inactive (Inactive == 1 in the material block) has been found in the GIS materials layer. Inactive materials cannot be assigned via a GIS material polygon layer.


Suggestions
Remove the inactive material ID from the GIS materials layer. Assign inactive materials directly in the .2dm mesh file instead.

title: Message 10162
text:
For GIS inputs either the MI PROJECTION (for mif) or SHP PROJECTION (for shp) must be specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
GIS inputs are configured but neither a MapInfo projection (MI Projection ==) nor a shapefile projection (SHP Projection ==) has been specified. One of these is required for TUFLOW FV to interpret the coordinate system of the GIS layers.


Suggestions
Add either MI Projection == (for mif/mid files) or SHP Projection == (for shp files) to the control file.

title: Message 10160
text:
Duplicated GIS polygon id \<polygon_id\>, in layer \<2d_sa_layer\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two polygons in the same GIS layer share the same name. Polygon IDs must be unique.


Suggestions
Open the named GIS layer and assign a unique name to each polygon. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the duplicated polygon.

title: Message 10158
text:
Unable to solve for specified inflow conditions at bc \<bc_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
During each timestep, TUFLOW FV uses a Newton-Raphson iteration to solve for the boundary flow conditions at inflow boundary conditions. This warning is raised when the iteration does not converge within the maximum number of steps. The simulation continues using the best available approximation from the iteration. This warning is often associated with automatic stage discharge QN boundary types.


Suggestions
This warning is often not indicative of a significant problem, particularly if the model results are otherwise reasonable. Check whether the model produces acceptable results at the affected boundary condition location.
If the warning appears frequently, check the boundary condition time series for abrupt changes in velocity or water level. If these occur try adjusting the boundary orientation to be perpendicular to the flow direction. Also ensure that the boundary condition is not overly constrained and accommodates the width of the floodplain.

title: Message 10156
text:
failed to find path



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The external nodestring path-finding algorithm could not find any adjacent mesh faces for a node, preventing the nodestring path from being completed. This indicates an inconsistency in the mesh topology at the affected node.


Suggestions
Check the mesh at the affected nodestring for degenerate or disconnected elements. Re-meshing the area or adding intermediate vertices to the nodestring may resolve the issue.
Check the 2d_ns GIS layer flag attribute. Ensure that ‘BD’ is only specfied for nodestrings that are intended to snap onto the edge of the mesh. Internal nodestrings, typically used for hydraulic structure connections or flux reporting should not be flagged as ‘BD’.

title: Message 10154
text:
ZLine Point not snapped to end of line



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The last vertex of the ZLine breakline has no elevation point snapped to it. When elevation points are used with a breakline the first and last vertices of the line must each have an elevation point snapped to them.


Suggestions
Add an elevation point snapped to the last vertex of the ZLine. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the unsnapped end vertex.

title: Message 10152
text:
Unexpected nodestring id



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Nodestring Polyline File == entry was specified without a nodestring ID. The ID is required to identify which polyline in the csv to use as the nodestring (syntax: Nodestring Polyline File == filename, id).


Suggestions
Add the nodestring ID as the second comma-separated argument to Nodestring Polyline File ==.
The Nodestring Polyline File == command is depreciated and it is recommended to use Read GIS Nodestring == with GIS integration.

title: Message 10150
text:
Surface layer (SIGMA=1.0) should not be explicitly specified in layer file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The csv file specified by Layer Face File == contains a sigma value of 1.0, which corresponds to the surface layer. TUFLOW FV adds the surface layer (SIGMA=1) automatically and it must not be included in the layer file. This check applies when Vertical Mesh Type == SIGMA.


Suggestions
Remove the SIGMA=1.0 entry from the layer file. Only interior sigma layer boundaries between 0 and 1 (exclusive) should be specified.

title: Message 10148
text:
SIGMA values must be between 0.0 and 1.0



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more sigma values in the csv file specified by Layer Face File == are outside the valid range of 0.0 to 1.0. This check applies when Vertical Mesh Type == SIGMA.


Suggestions
Check the SIGMA column in the layer file and ensure all values are between 0.0 and 1.0 exclusive. The bed layer (0.0) and surface layer (1.0) are added automatically and must not be included.

title: Message 10146
text:
Point \<point_id\> (\<x_coordinate\>, \<y_coordinate\>) is not located within model domain.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A point in a coordinate-format Cell Elevation File (X, Y, Z ) csv falls outside the model domain and will not be used to set cell elevations. The point location is plotted in the GIS messages layer.


Suggestions
Check that the Cell Elevation File coordinate projection matches the model domain. Points outside the mesh boundary are ignored and will not contribute to the bed elevation. When reviewing, point_id is the data row number in the csv file (excluding the header row, so point 1 will be on row 2 of the csv file).

title: Message 10144
text:
Out-of-range latitude [-90.,90.] encountered at node:\<node_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A mesh node has a latitude coordinate outside the valid range of −90° to 90°. This indicates the mesh coordinates are either in the wrong projection or the model is incorrectly configured to use spherical coordinates.


Suggestions
Check that the mesh coordinates are in geographic (latitude/longitude) decimal degrees. If the mesh is in a projected coordinate system set the model to use Cartesian coordinates in the control file. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the out-of-range node.

title: Message 10142
text:
Number of nodestrings must be less than or equal to \<max_nodestrings\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total number of nodestrings in the mesh exceeds the internal limit of 500. This is the combined number of nodestrings specified in the .2dm mesh file and via 2d_ns GIS layers.


Suggestions
Where possible, reduce the number of nodestrings in the mesh by simplifying or splitting the nodestring GIS data, or by removing nodestrings that are not needed for the current simulation. If the number of nodestrings cannot be reduced, contact support@tuflow.com to discuss options for increasing the internal limit.

title: Message 10140
text:
Nodestring \<nodestring_id\>, segment \<segment_number\> does not correspond to any model face.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A segment of the named nodestring does not correspond to any face in the mesh. This occurs when the nodestring vertices do not align with mesh nodes or when the nodestring extends outside the mesh domain.


Suggestions
Check that the nodestring GIS geometry aligns with the mesh. Ensure all nodestring vertices snap to mesh nodes and that the nodestring lies within the mesh boundary. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the failing segment.

title: Message 10138
text:
No points found in elevation polyline!



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No points were found in the elevation polyline CSV file matching the specified polyline ID. The optional polyline ID is the second comma-separated argument to Cell Elevation Polyline File ==.


Suggestions
Check that the ID column in the CSV file contains the specified polyline ID.
Cell Elevation Polyline File == is depreciated and it is recommended to use Read GIS Z Line and GIS integration.

title: Message 10136
text:
Negative area calculated for cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A zero or negative area was calculated for the mesh cell shown. This indicates an invalid cell where the vertices effectively form a straight line rather than a valid polygon.


Suggestions
Review the mesh at the location shown in the GIS messages output file and regenerate the mesh to resolve the invalid cell.
If the mesh cell looks reasonable, is the model a longitude/latitude model? If it is, ensure that Spherical == 1 is specified.

title: Message 10134
text:
Input arguments have not been constructed



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The mesh node ID array had not been constructed. This is an internal software issue and should not occur under normal circumstances.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please send through the log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10132
text:
GIS SA point input error



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A feature in the SA point GIS layer has more than one vertex. SA point inputs must be single-point features. This typically indicates a multipoint feature has been created in the GIS layer.


Suggestions
Open the 2d_sa layer in GIS and check for multipoint features. If multipoint geometry objects are identified, split them into single point geometry.
More generally, ensure the 2d_sa point layer has been generated from an empty GIS layer using TUFLOW FV’s model initialisation process. Using this process helps ensure that supported geometry types are used. See the model initialisation section of the TUFLOW FV User Manual for more information.

title: Message 10130
text:
Found \<2d_cell_count\> cell-centroids in polygon



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
