No mesh cell centroids were found inside the polygon. The polygon does not overlap any mesh cells and will have no effect.


Suggestions
Check that the polygon overlaps the mesh and is in the correct coordinate projection. Ensure the polygon covers at least one cell centroid.

title: Message 10128
text:
Nodestring overlap found between Nodestring ID=\<nodestring_id_1\> and Nodestring ID=\<nodestring_id_2\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two nodestrings share one or more common mesh faces. This can occur when nodestrings are digitised with overlapping segments or when two boundary condition lines cover the same mesh edges.


Suggestions
Review the two named nodestrings in the mesh or GIS editor and check for shared faces. If the overlap is unintentional adjust one or both nodestrings so they do not share any mesh faces. If both overlapping nodestrings are assigned as boundary conditions ERROR 10116 will also be raised.

title: Message 10126
text:
Fixed Grid Cellsize has not been specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A fixed grid mesh was requested but no cell size was provided. The Cell Size == keyword is required when using a fixed grid mesh.


Suggestions
Add Cell Size ==   to the control file to specify the fixed grid cell dimensions.

title: Message 10124
text:
Entire mesh has been set inactive. Check material types



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Every cell in the mesh has been marked as inactive, leaving no active computational domain. This typically means that all cells have been assigned material ID of 0 in the .2dm file or a a single material block exists with Inactive == 1 specification.


Suggestions
Check the material assignments in the mesh and review material blocks for Inactive == 1 specification. Ensure at least one material type maps to an active region of the domain.

title: Message 10122
text:
Elevation greater than 9999. encountered at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A cell with a bed elevation above 9999 m was detected after applying elevation data to the mesh. Values in this range are almost certainly NoData or null values from a bathymetry or DEM dataset that have been incorrectly applied to the mesh rather than masked.


Suggestions
Review the bathymetry and DEM source files for NoData regions. Ensure the NoData value is correctly specified in the source data so that cells without valid elevation data are not assigned unrealistic values.
Use the GIS messages output file to identify the affected cells and inspect the source data in those areas.

title: Message 10120
text:
Duplicate nodestring id: \<nodestring_id\> found in either 2dm or external nodestrings



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The same nodestring ID has been found more than once across the .2dm mesh and external nodestring GIS files. Nodestring IDs must be unique across all sources.


Suggestions
Check the .2dm file and all GIS nodestring layers for duplicate IDs and assign a unique ID to each nodestring. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the duplicated nodestring.

title: Message 10118
text:
Distance of zero encountered on breakline, check for cooincident vertices



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two consecutive vertices on a breakline are at the same or nearly identical coordinates, resulting in a zero distance between them. This prevents elevation interpolation along the breakline.


Suggestions
Open the breakline GIS layer and check for coincident or duplicate vertices. Remove or merge any duplicate vertices and rerun the simulation. The GIS output shows a point on the affected breakline.

title: Message 10116
text:
Found overlapping boundary condition nodestrings



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more pairs of boundary condition nodestrings share mesh faces. Overlapping boundary condition nodestrings are not permitted. Each overlapping pair has been reported individually by the preceding WARNING 10128 messages which include the nodestring IDs and the location of the overlap in the GIS messages output file.


Suggestions
Review the preceding WARNING 10128 messages and the GIS messages output file to identify the location of each overlap. Modify the boundary condition nodestrings so that no two nodestrings share the same mesh face.

title: Message 10114
text:
triangle index error



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more triangle index values in the TIN file TRI block are zero, indicating a missing or invalid vertex reference. Triangle indices must be 1-based and refer to a valid entry in the VERT block.


Suggestions
Check the TIN file TRI block for zero or missing index values and correct them.

title: Message 10112
text:
fvopen argument combination not supported



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unsupported combination of format and access arguments was passed to the internal file open routine. This is an internal error that indicates an unexpected call to the file handler.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please send through the log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10110
text:
Not enough vertices in TIN file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The TIN file specifies fewer than 3 vertices in a VERT block. A valid TIN requires at least 3 vertices to form a triangle.


Suggestions
Check the TIN file and ensure the VERT block contains at least 3 valid vertices.

title: Message 10108
text:
File name has not been specified or is blank.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A file open was attempted with a blank or empty filename. This indicates that a required filename was not set before the file operation was called.


Suggestions
Check the control file for any input file paths that are missing or blank.

title: Message 10106
text:
Data is stored as 8 bit integers, repack as 16 bit



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The grid file specified by Cell Elevation Grid contains data stored as 8-bit integers. TUFLOW FV requires grd files to use 16-bit integer data precision.


Suggestions
Re-export the grid file with 16-bit integer precision and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10104
text:
face mesh%face incompatible sizes



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of faces in the face object does not match the number of faces in the mesh. This is an internal consistency check that should not occur under normal circumstances.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please send through the log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10102
text:
Structure A-side and B-side flows are numerically inconsistent. Structure \<structure\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The A-side and B-side flows computed for a hydraulic structure are numerically inconsistent, indicating that flux is not being conserved across the structure during the simulation.


Suggestions
This issue is typically associated with model instability, or incorrect structure configuration, particularly for hQh Matrix flux functions. Check the structure definition and nodestring geometry for the reported structure. Ensure the nodestring is correctly assigned to both sides of the structure and that the structure parameters are valid. The GIS output shows the location of the affected structure.

title: Message 10100
text:
unexpected mode specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unexpected mode value was encountered in the CFL output routine. This is an internal software issue and should not occur under normal circumstances.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please send through the log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10098
text:
Water surface is less than \<fixed_zlayer_depth_tolerance\>m above top zlayer at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
In 3D z-coordinate models Vertical Mesh Type == Z, the water surface at each active cell must remain above the top fixed z-layer boundary by at least the fixed z-layer depth tolerance. This error occurs when that condition is violated at the cell shown. Note that any surface sigma layers above the top fixed z-layer are not considered by this check.


Suggestions
Check the Layer Face File == to ensure the top fixed z-layer elevation is set below the expected minimum water surface across the domain. If the error occurs during model start up or early in the simulation, check that the initial water surface specification is consistent with the z-layer configuration. If the error occurs later during the simution, check that the water level has not lowered due to water level boundary conditions, wind or atomspheric pressure forcing setdown, or due to evaporation and flow extractions.
The depth tolerance used in this check is the dry depth set via the from Cell Wet/Dry Depths == command.

title: Message 10096
text:
Water surface and/or velocity magnitude has exceeded limits in 2D cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when using the GPU solver. It occurs when either the water surface elevation or the velocity magnitude at the specified 2D cell has exceeded the configured Stability Limits ==. Unlike the CPU solver, the GPU kernel reports both checks as a single combined message.


Suggestions
Ensure the stability limits in Stability Limits == reflect the expected flow conditions. The first argument is the water surface upper bound (mRL or ftRL) and the second is the velocity upper bound (m/s or ft/s).
The simulation time at which the error occurs may help to diagnose the issue. If the error occurs early in the simulation or at initialisation, it is likely a model configuration, initial condition or boundary condition mismatch. Check that the water surface upper bound exceeds the maximum topographic/bathymetric elevation, this is a common cause of error. If the error occurs later and the model configuration appears correct, the region surrounding the offending 2D cell warrants further investigation.
For model instability, review the model setup in the vicinity of the cell shown in the GIS messages output file. Common causes include a timestep that is too large for the mesh resolution, poor mesh quality near the affected cell, and extreme or incorrectly specified boundary conditions.
While the error will be reported at the first cell that exceeds the stability limit, the root cause may originate from a nearby cell. To track where instability begins add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to the error. See ERROR 10097 for an example output block.
The command Write Restart At Time == can also be useful to start a follow-up run close to the time of the error.

title: Message 10094
text:
Velocity has exceeded stability limit \<velocity_stability_limit\> (m/s or ft/s) at 2D cell \<2d_cell_id\> (3D cell \<3d_cell_id\> - vertical layer \<layer_id\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The velocity at the 3D cell shown has exceeded the configured stability limit during the simulation. This may indicate numerical instability which has caused the solution to diverge at this location. The velocity stability limit is the second argument set using Stability Limits ==. The 2D cell, 3D cell and vertical layer where the limit was exceeded are all reported.


Suggestions
The stability limits can be adjusted using the Stability Limits == command in the model control file. Ensure that the specified velocity limit argument reflects the expected flow conditions being investigated. A velocity limit of 10 m/s is commonly used.
The simulation time at which the error occurs may help to diagnose the issue. If the error occurs early in the simulation or at initialisation, it is likely a model configuration, initial condition or boundary condition mismatch. If the error occurs later during the simulation and the model configuration appears correct, the region surrounding the offending 2D cell(s) warrants further investigation for instabilities.
For model instability, review the model setup in the vicinity of the cell shown in the GIS messages output file. Common causes include a timestep that is too large for the mesh resolution, poor mesh quality near the affected cell and extreme or incorrectly specified boundary conditions.
The vertical layer reported can help identify whether the instability is occurring near the surface, at depth or at the bed. Check the layer structure and any depth-varying boundary conditions near the affected cell.
While the error will be reported at the first cell that exceeds the specified stability limit, the root case may originate from a different cell, typically close by. To track where velocity divergence begins, it may be useful to add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to when the error occurs. For example, if the model crashes at 02/12/2008 21:15:36:
Output == NetCDF 
    Suffix == CHK                             ! For checking
    Output Parameters == h, v                 ! Water level, velocity
    Start Output == 02/12/2008 21:15:00       ! Time close to the error occurrence
    Final Output == 02/12/2008 21:17:00       ! Time immediately after the crash, mainly for safety so the model cannot continue writing high temporal resolution output AND FILL UP RESULT STORAGE. BE CAREFUL!!!!
    Output Interval == 1                      ! (s) High temporal resolution output to help track initial cell where instability starts and propagation
End Output
This block writes water level and velocity at 1 second intervals (0 will use the model timestep if higher temporal resolution is required) in a narrow window around the error. Stepping through the output in time allows identification of the initial cell where instability begins and its propagation path.
The command Write Restart At Time == can also be useful to start a follow-up run close to the time of the error.

title: Message 10092
text:
Timestep has gone negative, possibly due to a negative cell dZ



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the CFL-based adaptive timestep calculation produces a negative value, possibly due to a negative cell layer thickness (dZ).


Suggestions
Review the model near the GIS message location for unusual velocities or flow behaviour leading up to the error. Review the mesh quality in the region near the error. Review the model timestepping in the log file and CFL diagnostic output csv files for any evidence of other cells with low minimum or average timesteps.
To track where instability begins, add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to the error. See ERROR 10097 for an example output block.

title: Message 10090
text:
Provided coordinates are outside the region.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The coordinates specified for the Auto Terminate == command do not fall within any mesh cell. TUFLOW FV uses these coordinates to locate the 2D cell to monitor for automatic simulation termination. The provided coordinates are shown as a point in the GIS messages output file.


Suggestions
Check the coordinates specified in Auto Terminate ==. The point must lie within the model mesh domain. Verify that the coordinates are in the correct projection and units for the model.

title: Message 10088
text:
GPU Hardware target currently only supports up to \<max_vertical_layers\> vertical cell layers



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the number of vertical cell layers in the model exceeds the limit supported by the GPU hardware target. The maximum supported layer count is shown as <max_vertical_layers> in the message text.


Suggestions
The number of vertical layers is defined by the Layer Face File command for Vertical Mesh Type == Sigma and both the Layer Face File and Surface Sigma Layers commands for Vertical Mesh Type == Z. Review these commands and reduce the number of vertical layers to within the stated limit.

title: Message 10086
text:
Duplicate grid labels are not permitted.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during domain construction when two or more Grid Definition or Grid Definition File blocks have the same label. Grid labels must be unique.


Suggestions
Check all Grid Definition and Grid Definition File blocks and ensure each has a distinct label.

title: Message 10084
text:
Nodestring ID \<nodestring_id\>'s length of \<nodestring_length\> \<units\> exceeds culvert/s width of \<culvert_width\> \<units\> by \<excess_length\> \<units\>. Check if nodestring/mesh can be modified to better match culvert width.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total length of the nodestring structure connection associated with the culvert exceeds the total width of the culvert structure (total barrels x pipe diamater or box culvert width). Structure calculations use nodestring-averaged hydraulic parameters where each cell face in the nodestring is weighted by its length and depth. When the nodestring extends beyond the culvert width additional cell faces outside the culvert opening are included in the average which may not be representative of the flow conditions at the structure.


Suggestions
Where possible refine the mesh in the vicinity of the culvert so that the nodestring length more closely matches the culvert width. Check that the culvert dimensions and number of barrels specified in the culvert data are correct. A small excess in nodestring length relative to culvert width may be unavoidable depending on mesh resolution and is generally acceptable.

title: Message 10082
text:
Culvert/s \<culvert_id\>'s width of \<culvert_width\> \<units\> exceeds nodestring length by \<nodestring_length\> \<units\>. Increase nodestring length to ensure adequate 1D/2D connection width.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total width of the culvert barrels is greater than the length of the associated nodestring. The nodestring defines the 1D/2D connection at the culvert and must be at least as long as the total culvert width to ensure the full flow area is connected to the 2D domain.


Suggestions
Extend the nodestring so its total length is at least equal to the total culvert width. The total culvert width is the number of barrels multiplied by the barrel width. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the culvert nodestring. In some cases the model mesh may need to be adjusted to improve flow path representation at the culvert inlet or outlet.

title: Message 10080
text:
Culvert downstream invert is less than ground elevation, ID \<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV checks each culvert’s invert elevations against the bed elevation of the mesh cells in the culvert’s downstream connection (nodestring or zone) during model initialisation. This message is raised when the downstream invert elevation is lower than the minimum bed elevation in those cells, meaning the culvert opening sits below the ground surface as represented in the mesh.
The severity is controlled by the Culvert Invert Check == command. It is raised as an error by default and can be downgraded to a warning by setting Culvert Invert Check == WARNING.


Suggestions
Check the downstream invert elevation specified for the culvert in the culvert definition file and compare it against the bed elevation of the mesh at the downstream connection. The invert elevation should be at or above the ground surface as defined by the mesh bathymetry.
If the discrepancy is small and physically reasonable (for example, where the mesh resolution means bed elevations are coarser than the culvert geometry), set Culvert Invert Check == WARNING in the control file to allow the simulation to proceed with a warning rather than an error.

title: Message 10078
text:
"n_or_n_F" is unusually high (>1.0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the n_or_n_F value for culvert <culvert_id> exceeds 1.0. A Manning’s ‘n’ value above 1.0 is erroneously high and likely indicates a data entry error.


Suggestions
Check the n_or_n_F column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and confirm the intended value.

title: Message 10076
text:
"Width" definition error (<=0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the Width value for culvert <culvert_id> is zero or negative. Width must be a positive value.


Suggestions
Check the Width column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value.

title: Message 10074
text:
"Len_or_ANA" definition error (<=0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the Len_or_ANA value for culvert <culvert_id> is zero or negative. The culvert length must be a positive value.


Suggestions
Check the Len_or_ANA column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value.

title: Message 10072
text:
"Height" definition error (<=0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the height value for culvert <culvert_id> is zero or negative. Height must be a positive value.


Suggestions
Check the height column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value.

title: Message 10070
text:
"Blockage" definition error (<0.0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the blockage value for culvert <culvert_id> is negative. Blockage must be a percentage in the range 0–100.


Suggestions
Check the blockage column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value to a valid percentage.

title: Message 10068
text:
Unknown vertical coordinate type \<vertical_coord_type\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when an unrecognised value is given for the Sample Vertical Coordinate Type command in a hydraulic structure optional control block. The value read is shown as <vertical_coord_type> in the message text.


Suggestions
Set Sample Vertical Coordinate Type to one of the accepted values: Elevation, Depth, Sigma, or Height.

title: Message 10066
text:
TUFLOW WQ Module requires simulation of temperature. Exiting



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the water quality module is selected but temperature simulation is not enabled in the model control file. The WQ module requires temperature to be active.


Suggestions
Add Include Temperature == 1,  to the model control file, where <coupling> is 1 to couple temperature to density or 0 to decouple.

title: Message 10064
text:
TUFLOW WQ Module requires simulation of heat. Exiting



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the water quality module is selected but heat simulation is not enabled in the model control file. The WQ module requires heat to be active.


Suggestions
Add Include Heat == 1 to the model control file and ensure the required meteorological boundary conditions are configured to support heat simulation.

title: Message 10062
text:
Start time MUST be specified, even when using a restart file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Start Time == command was not found in the main fvc file, or any include files or event files. TUFLOW FV requires an explicit start time in all simulations, including those that use a restart file. The command is required to place an initial bound for temporal extrapolation boundary data checks.


Suggestions
Add a Start Time == command to the model fvc file with the intended simulation start time.

title: Message 10060
text:
Number of sediment fractions (Nsed) is greater than maximum allowed (\<max_sed_fractions\>).



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during control file processing when the number of sediment fractions defined in the sediment control file exceeds the compiled maximum, shown as <max_sed_fractions> in the message text.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of sediment fractions to within the stated limit. Contact support@tuflow.com if the limit needs to be increased for your application.

title: Message 10058
text:
It is recommended to use Sigma 3D vertical layering (not Z or Z-Sigma) when sediment morphologic update is enabled.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This warning is raised when sediment morphologic update is enabled alongside Z or Z-Sigma vertical layering. Sigma 3D layering is the recommended vertical discretisation for models with an active bed morphology.


Suggestions
In the model control file, use Vertical Mesh Type == Sigma to enable Sigma 3D vertical layering.

title: Message 10056
text:
Error in water quality model



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unspecified error occurred in the water quality model during initialisation.


Suggestions
Check the model log file for surrounding water quality messages. Review the water quality control file and water quality log file for further information.

title: Message 10054
text:
Dry depth will never make dry cells



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The dry depth specified by Cell Wet/Dry Depths is zero or negative. A dry depth of zero or less will never cause cells to be treated as dry.


Suggestions
Check the Cell Wet/Dry Depths setting in the control file and set the dry depth to a small positive value.

title: Message 10052
text:
Cell 3D Depth is below zero. It will not have any effect



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Cell 3D Depth == is zero or negative, so it will have no effect on the simulation.


Suggestions
Check the Cell 3D Depth == command and ensure a positive depth value is specified.

title: Message 10050
text:
Imperial/US Customary/English Units are not yet supported for \<model_feature\>. Please use Units == Metric



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The model feature shown in the message does not support Imperial/US Customary units.


Suggestions
Set Units == Metric in the control file, or disable the model feature that triggered this error.

title: Message 10048
text:
material group specified in control file is not consistent with geometry file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A material group number specified in the control file exceeds the number of material groups defined in the geometry file. The material group numbers in the control file must correspond to groups that exist in the mesh.


Suggestions
Check the material group numbers in the Material == blocks of the control file and verify they match the material group IDs defined in the mesh geometry file.

title: Message 10046
text:
error echoing cell geometry \<internal_file_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred while writing cell geometry data to a debug echo file. This is raised when a write operation fails on an open output file during model initialisation.


Suggestions
Check that there is sufficient disk space available and that the output directory is accessible and not write protected.
Disable geometry csv echoing by either setting Echo Geometry == 0 or Echo Geometry CSV == 0 in the control file.

title: Message 10044
text:
code block not yet implemented on GPU



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A model feature that requires this code path has been activated but the corresponding GPU implementation is not yet available.


Suggestions
Run the simulation on CPU instead of GPU, using Hardware == CPU, or disable the model feature that triggered this error.

title: Message 10042
text:
NaN detected in density field in cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was detected in the computed density field at the 2D cell shown. This indicates a numerical issue in the equation of state calculation, typically caused by invalid temperature or salinity values being used as inputs.


Suggestions
Check the temperature and salinity map outputs, boundary conditions and initial conditions near the reported cell for unrealistic or missing values. The cell location can be identified in the GIS messages output file. If temperature is enabled with atmospheric heat exchange, check that input meterological data is reasonable and does not contain non-physical values.

title: Message 10040
text:
\<bc_header_entry\> size is not compatible with \<bc_header_entry\>, \<bc_header_entry\> /or \<bc_header_entry\> dimensions.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A variable in a OBC_CURT or SCALAR_CURT boundary condition netCDF file has dimensions that are not compatible with the spatial, vertical and time dimension variables in the same file.


Suggestions
Check the netCDF file for the curtain boundary condition. The variable shown in the message must have dimensions matching those of the spatial coordinate, vertical coordinate and time variables. Regenerate the file if the dimensions are inconsistent.

title: Message 10038
text:
error executing wave timestep, check wave model log files



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A wave model error occurred during execution of a coupled wave model timestep.


Suggestions
Review the wave model output log and error files for details on the error.

title: Message 10036
text:
Unexpected temporal output return



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unexpected internal software error has occurred when checking temporal alignment checks.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and provide the model log file from the offending simulation. This error is unexpected and should not occur in normal operation. The log file will assist TUFLOW Support in identifying the cause of the error.

title: Message 10034
text:
Unexpected temporal extrapolation type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The temporal extrapolation check type specified for a boundary condition is not recognised. Valid values are ERROR and WARNING.


Suggestions
Check the Temporal Extrapolation Check == command in the boundary condition block and the Global Temporal Extrapolation Check == command in the control file. Both commands accept only ERROR or WARNING as valid values.

title: Message 10032
text:
Unexpected nodestring id \<nodestring_id\> in bc \<bc_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV raises this error during mesh initialisation when a boundary condition references a nodestring ID that does not exist in the mesh. The boundary condition number shown in the message corresponds to the order in which boundary conditions are listed in the control file.


Suggestions
Check that the nodestring ID referenced by boundary condition <bc_id> exactly matches an ID in the nodestring geometry inputs. ID matching is not case-sensitive. Verify there are no typos or extra whitespace.

title: Message 10030
text:
OBC_GRID and SCALAR_GRID boundary conditions must be linked with a grid with boundary nodestrings mapped (use command "BOUNDARY GRIDMAP == 1")



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
OBC_GRID and SCALAR_GRID boundary condition types require the associated grid to have boundary nodestrings mapped. The grid referenced by this boundary condition does not have boundary nodestring mapping enabled.


Suggestions
Add Boundary Gridmap == 1 to the Grid Definition == or Grid Definition File == block associated with this boundary condition.

title: Message 10028
text:
No polygon corresponding to ID, \<polygon_id\>, found in CSV file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A polygon boundary condition references a polygon ID that cannot be found in the csv polygon file. The polygon ID is matched against the ID column in the file. ID matching is not case-sensitive.


Suggestions
Check that the polygon ID specified in the boundary condition matches an ID in the ID column of the csv polygon file. Verify there are no typographical errors or extra whitespace in either the boundary condition definition or the csv file.
The use of polygon BCs has been superseded by the use of GIS 2d_sa polygon layers. If possible, consider using a GIS polygon layer instead of a csv polygon file.

title: Message 10026
text:
Must specify a bc update time for a wave_coupled bc.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A coupled wave boundary condition requires a BC update time interval to be specified but none has been provided. The update time controls how frequently the wave model exchanges data with TUFLOW FV.


Suggestions
Specify the coupling update interval using one of the following:

Add a BC Default Update DT == command at the top of the control file to set a default update interval for all boundary conditions, or
Add a BC Update dt == command within the wave boundary condition block to set the interval for that boundary condition only.

The update interval should match the SWAN model computation timestep.

title: Message 10024
text:
Moving BC (bc_id=\<bc_id\>) is currently outside model domain.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A moving source boundary condition currently has a position that falls outside the model domain. TUFLOW FV will not apply the boundary at this timestep but will continue the simulation. The GIS messages output file will show the last attempted position of the boundary to help identify where it left the domain.


Suggestions
Check the trajectory of the moving source boundary condition against the model domain extent. If the source is expected to re-enter the domain later in the simulation the warning can be ignored for the period it is outside. If the source should remain within the domain check that the input position coordinates and timing are correct.

title: Message 10022
text:
Error processing vertical distribution file. NaN detected.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was detected when reading a vertical distribution file for a 3D boundary condition. The file will be specified in a boundary condition block using the Vertical Distribution File command. The file must contain valid numeric values in both the position column (elevation, depth, sigma or height) and the weight column.


Suggestions
Open the vertical distribution csv file and check for missing or invalid values in either column. All rows must contain valid numeric data. Common causes include empty cells, text in numeric columns or incorrect delimiter formatting.
This error is not related to missing or incorrect column names. If the vertical distribution file column names are incorrect, ERROR 10279 will be raised.

title: Message 10020
text:
Error initialising external wave Model



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred while initialising the external wave model coupling interface. This is raised when the external wave model library fails to initialise during boundary condition setup.


Suggestions
Contact TUFLOW Support via support@tuflow.com and attach the TUFLOW log file from the offending simulation.

title: Message 10018
text:
Could not find a matching grid id/label



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A grid boundary condition type references a Grid Definition Label that does not match any of existing Grid Definition or Grid Definition File blocks specified in the model. TUFLOW FV searches all grid definition blocks for a Grid Definition Label matching the one specified in the boundary condition definition BC == command.


Suggestions
Check that the grid label specified in the boundary condition definition matches the label of one of the grid files referenced in the control file. Grid labels are case-insensitive.

title: Message 10016
text:
wind stress model not recognised, needs to be 1 to 3



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Wind Stress Model == is not recognised. Valid values are 1 (Wu), 2 (Constant) and 3 (Kondo).


Suggestions
Check the Wind Stress Model == command in the control file and set it to 1, 2 or 3. For more information on the selection of Wind Stress Model, refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10014
text:
short wave radiation heat transfer model requires incident short wave radiation defined by the user



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Shortwave Radiation Model == 1 requires a shortwave radiation boundary condition but one has not been provided.


Suggestions
Ensure that a SW_RAD (or SW_RAD_GRID) boundary condition is defined in the model. For more information on the selection of Shortwave Radiation Model, refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10012
text:
long wave radiation heat transfer model requires air temperature defined by the user



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Longwave Radiation Model == 3 and Longwave Radiation Model == 4 require an air temperature boundary condition but one has not been provided.


Suggestions
Ensure that an AIR_TEMP (or AIR_TEMP_GRID) boundary condition is defined in the model.

title: Message 10010
text:
latent heat transfer model not recognised, needs to be 1 or 2



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Latent Heat Model == is not recognised. Valid values are 1 and 2.


Suggestions
Check the Latent Heat Model == command in the control file and set it to 1 or 2. Refer to the [TUFLOW FV User Manual](https://docs.tuflow.com/fv/manual/latest/) for further information on the selection of Latent Heat Model.

title: Message 10008
text:
Wind speed not defined by the user. Wind velocity assumed to be null



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The selected latent heat transfer model requires wind speed data but no W10 or W10_GRID boundary condition has been provided. TUFLOW FV assumes zero wind velocity and continues the simulation.


Suggestions
If wind data is available for the simulation period, add a W10 or W10_GRID boundary condition. Note that zero wind speed will affect the latent and sensible heat transfer calculations.

title: Message 10006
text:
Radiation heat transfer model requires air temperature and relative humidity defined by the user



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The selected radiation model requires both air temperature and relative humidity boundary conditions but one or both have not been provided.


Suggestions
Ensure that both an AIR_TEMP (or AIR_TEMP_GRID) and a REL_HUM (or REL_HUM_GRID) boundary condition are defined in the model.

title: Message 10004
text:
Long wave radiation heat transfer model requires long wave radiation defined by the user



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The long wave radiation model selected by Longwave Radiation Model == requires a direct long wave radiation boundary condition that has not been provided.


Suggestions
Check that the boundary conditions supplied match the model selected:

Model 1 (direct net long wave radiation) requires an LW_NET or LW_NET_GRID boundary condition.
Model 2 (incident long wave radiation) requires an LW_RAD or LW_RAD_GRID boundary condition.

title: Message 10002
text:
Cloud cover not defined by the user. Clear skies assumed for radiation heat transfer model



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The selected radiation model can use cloud cover data but no CLOUD or CLOUD_GRID boundary condition has been provided. TUFLOW FV assumes clear sky conditions and continues the simulation.


Suggestions
If cloud cover data is available for the simulation period, add a CLOUD or CLOUD_GRID boundary condition to the model. If clear sky conditions are a reasonable assumption, this warning can be ignored.

title: Message 10000
text:
Memory allocation failure.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV was unable to allocate the memory required at this point in the simulation. This typically indicates that the system does not have sufficient free RAM to run the model.


Suggestions
Ensure the system has sufficient free RAM for the model size. If memory is limited try reducing the number of 2D mesh cells and/or the number of vertical layers if running in 3D. If the error occurs on a system with adequate memory contact support@tuflow.com.

title: Message 10001
text:
Memory deallocation failure.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV was unable to release previously allocated memory. This typically indicates a system memory issue or an internal error.


Suggestions
Ensure the system has sufficient free RAM for the model size. If the error persists contact support@tuflow.com.

title: Message 10003
text:
Heat should not be included if temperature is not simulated



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Atmospheric heat exchange is enabled via Include Heat == but temperature is not being simulated. Atmospheric heat exchange requires temperature to be an active constituent in the simulation.


Suggestions
Either enable temperature simulation using the Include Temperature == command, or disable heat transfer by setting Include Heat == 0. Both settings must be consistent for the model to run.

title: Message 10005
text:
NaN detected in cell, \<2d_cell_id\>, layer, \<layer_id\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was detected in the computed atmospheric heat flux at the 2D cell and vertical layer shown. This indicates a numerical issue in the heat transfer computation at that location.


Suggestions
Check the atmospheric boundary condition data (air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and radiation inputs) for unrealistic or missing values near the time the error occurs. NaN values in the heat flux typically indicate extreme or invalid input data being passed to the radiation or turbulent heat transfer calculations.
The cell location can be identified in the GIS messages output file.

title: Message 10007
text:
Sum of shortwave bed absorption coefficients must not be greater than 1.0.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sum of the two short wave radiation bed absorption coefficients set by Shortwave Radiation Bed Absorption == exceeds 1.0. The two values represent the fractions of short wave radiation absorbed by the sediment layer and the bottom water column layer respectively. Their combined total cannot exceed 1.0.


Suggestions
Check the Shortwave Radiation Bed Absorption == command and ensure the two values sum to 1.0 or less.

title: Message 10009
text:
day_of_the_year requires tform == 1



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The solar radiation calculation requires the calendar date to determine the day of the year and solar declination angle. This is only possible when the model uses a date-based time format. The current model is using decimal hours time format (Time Format == HOURS), which does not contain calendar date information.


Suggestions
Change the time format to use calendar dates by setting Time Format == ISODATE in the control file. Update Start Time ==, End Time == and all boundary condition time references to use the dd/mm/yyyy HH:MM:SS format accordingly.

title: Message 10011
text:
latent heat transfer model requires air temperature and relative humidity defined by the user



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Latent Heat Model == 1 and Latent Heat Model == 2 require both air temperature and relative humidity boundary conditions but one or both have not been provided.


Suggestions
Ensure that both an AIR_TEMP (or AIR_TEMP_GRID) and a REL_HUM (or REL_HUM_GRID) boundary condition are defined in the model.

title: Message 10013
text:
long wave radiation model not recognised, needs to be 1 to 2



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Longwave Radiation Model == is not recognised. Valid values are 1 to 5.


Suggestions
Check the Longwave Radiation Model == command in the control file and set it to a value between 1 and 5. For more information on the selection of Longwave Radiation Model, refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10015
text:
short wave radiation model not recognised, needs to be 1 or 2



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Short Wave Radiation Model == is not recognised.


Suggestions
Check the Short Wave Radiation Model == command in the control file and set it to 1 or 2. Refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual for further information on model selection.

title: Message 10017
text:
Boundary condition (bc_id=\<bc_id\>) is located outside model domain!



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The location specified for the boundary condition falls outside the model domain. The boundary condition will not be applied to any mesh cells.


Suggestions
Check the coordinates or GIS input used to locate the boundary condition and ensure they fall within the model mesh. If using a GIS SA point check the file projection and that the point overlaps the mesh.

title: Message 10019
text:
Current timestep is not included in transport file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The transport file does not cover the full simulation period. This error is raised when the current simulation timestep falls before the start or after the end of the time series in the transport file. A 10 second tolerance is applied at each end before the error is raised.


Suggestions
Check that the transport file time series spans the full simulation period from start time to end time. Extend the file by regenerating the transport file for a longer period, or adjust the simulation start and end times to match the transport file time series.

title: Message 10021
text:
Error initialising external wave model grid



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The external wave model grid referenced by the boundary condition could not be found or has zero dimensions. This is raised when the grid label specified in the wave boundary condition does not match any grid specification loaded for the model.


Suggestions
Check that the grid label specified in the wave boundary condition matches a Grid Definition == or Grid Definition File == block in the control file. Ensure the grid specification is correctly defined.

title: Message 10023
text:
Error while closing external wave model



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred while closing the external wave model at the end of the simulation. This is raised when the wave model library reports a failure during its shutdown and deallocation sequence.


Suggestions
Check the model log for additional detail written before this error. This is most likely an issue with the external wave model library rather than the TUFLOW FV model configuration. Contact support@tuflow.com if the error persists and attach the TUFLOW log file from the offending simulation.

title: Message 10025
text:
Model start or end time is outside of BC \<bc_id\> temporal extent.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The simulation start or end time falls outside the temporal extent of the boundary condition data. By default TUFLOW FV does not extrapolate boundary condition data beyond the available time range.


Suggestions
Extend the boundary condition time series to cover the full simulation period. Alternatively set the bc block command Temporal Extrapolation Check == WARNING on the individual boundary condition.

title: Message 10027
text:
No point corresponding to ID, \<point_id\>, found in any GIS SA file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A boundary condition block references a named point that could not be found in any of the GIS SA files loaded by the model. The point name in the boundary condition must match the Name attribute of a point in one of the loaded GIS SA files.


Suggestions
Check that the point ID shown in the message matches the Name attribute of a point in the GIS SA files. Name matching is not case sensitive. Verify that the correct GIS SA files are referenced in the model control file and that the file containing the point has been loaded.

title: Message 10029
text:
No polygon corresponding to ID, \<polygon_id\>, found in any GIS SA file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A boundary condition block references a named polygon that could not be found in any of the GIS SA files loaded by the model. The polygon name in the boundary condition must match the Name attribute of a polygon in one of the loaded GIS SA files.


Suggestions
Check that the polygon ID shown in the message matches the Name attribute of a polygon in the GIS SA files. Name matching is not case sensitive. Verify that the correct GIS SA files are referenced in the model control file and that the file containing the polygon has been loaded.

title: Message 10031
text:
Unexpected bc type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The boundary condition type specified is not recognised. This can occur when an invalid or unsupported boundary_type value is provided for the BC == boundary_type command in a boundary condition block.


Suggestions
Check the BC == command in the boundary condition block for typographical errors and verify it is a supported boundary condition type for the current version of TUFLOW FV.

title: Message 10033
text:
Unexpected subtype for flow boundary condition



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The subtype specified for a flow boundary condition is not recognised. Valid subtypes differ between boundary condition types.


Suggestions
Check the Subtype == value in the boundary condition block. Refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual simulation class boundary condition sections for a list of valid subtypes for the boundary condition type being used.

title: Message 10035
text:
Unrecognised boundary condition type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The boundary condition type specified in the control file is not recognised. This is raised when the BC Type == keyword does not match any supported boundary condition type.


Suggestions
Check the BC Type == command in the boundary condition block for typographical errors and verify it is a supported boundary condition type for the current version of TUFLOW FV.

title: Message 10037
text:
Wave_coupled bc is only compatible with ISOtime simulations.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The coupled wave boundary condition requires the model to use a calendar date based time format. The model is currently using decimal hours time format which does not contain calendar date information required for the wave coupling.


Suggestions
Change the time format to use calendar dates by setting Time Format == ISODATE in the control file. Update Start Time ==, End Time == and all boundary condition time references to use the dd/mm/yyyy HH:MM:SS format accordingly.

title: Message 10039
text:
\<bc_header_entry\> size is not compatible with \<bc_header_entry\> /or \<bc_header_entry\> dimensions.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A variable in a OBC_CURT boundary condition netCDF file has dimensions that are not compatible with the spatial and time dimension variables in the same file.


Suggestions
Check the netCDF file for the OBC_CURT boundary condition. The variable shown in the message must have dimensions matching those of the spatial coordinate and time variables. Regenerate the file if the dimensions are inconsistent.

title: Message 10041
text:
\<bc_data\> variable is stationary (no time dimension)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The named variable was found in the netCDF boundary condition file but does not include a time dimension. TUFLOW FV will treat the variable as a constant value for the duration of the simulation.


Suggestions
If the boundary condition is intended to vary over time check that the netCDF variable includes a time dimension and that the time values in the file cover the simulation period. If a constant boundary value is appropriate then the warning can be ignored.
This warning is common for the WL_CURT boundary condition, CHAINAGE input variable. If this is the case, the warning can typically be ignored.

title: Message 10043
text:
Unknown initial condition specification



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The initial condition type is not recognised.


Suggestions
Check the initial condition commands in the control file for typographical errors and verify that the initial condition type is supported. There are a range of initial condition commands available, as specified in the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10045
text:
depth has gone negative at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
During a depth update step, the net outward flux at a 2D cell would result in a negative water depth. Only the first cell where this occurs is reported. This indicates a numerical stability issue in which the outgoing flux exceeds the available water volume at that cell.


Suggestions
The simulation time at which the error occurs may help to diagnose the issue. If the error occurs early in the simulation or at initialisation, it is likely a model configuration, initial condition or boundary condition mismatch. If the error occurs later during the simulation and the model configuration appears correct, the region surrounding the offending 2D cell warrants further investigation for instabilities.
Common causes of instabilty include a timestep that is too large for the mesh resolution or flow conditions, very shallow cells with high velocities, poor mesh quality near the affected cell and abrupt changes in bed topography or boundary conditions.
While the error will be reported at the first cell that goes negative, the root case may originate from a different cell, typically close by. To track where instability begins, it may be useful to add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to when the error occurs. For example, if the model crashes at 02/12/2008 21:15:36:
Output == NetCDF 
    Suffix == CHK                             ! For checking
    Output Parameters == h, v                 ! Water level, velocity
    Start Output == 02/12/2008 21:15:00       ! Time close to the error occurrence
    Final Output == 02/12/2008 21:17:00       ! Time immediately after the crash, mainly for safety so the model cannot continue writing high temporal resolution output ! CARE SHOULD BE EXERCISED TO AVOID LARGE FILE OUTPUT SIZE
    Output Interval == 1                      ! (s) High temporal resolution output to help track initial cell where instability starts and propagation
End Output
This block writes water level and velocity at 1 second intervals (0 will use the model timestep if higher temporal resolution is required) in a narrow window around the error. Stepping through the output in time allows identification of the initial cell where instability begins and its propagation path.
The command Write Restart At Time == can also be useful to start a follow-up run close to the time of the error.
If investigations do not uncover any model or mesh setup issues, the user can experiment with the CFL == and Timesteps Limit == commands. Refer to the computation timestep section of the TUFLOW FV User Manual for further guidance on timestep selection.

title: Message 10047
text:
incompatible cell and mesh object sizes



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of cells in the cell object does not match the number of cells in the mesh object. This indicates an internal inconsistency in the model data structures and is not caused by user input.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com with the model log file if this error occurs.

title: Message 10049
text:
number of material groups specified in cell object is not consistent with mesh object



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of material groups in the cell object exceeds the number defined in the mesh object. This indicates an internal inconsistency in the model data structures and is not caused by user input.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com with the model log file if this error occurs.

title: Message 10051
text:
A sediment control file has been specified, but 'Include Sediment == 0,0'



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A sediment control file has been specified in the control file but sediment transport is not enabled (Include Sediment == 0, 0).


Suggestions
Either enable sediment transport using Include Sediment == 1, 0 or remove the sediment control file specification from the control file.

title: Message 10053
text:
Could not determine number of sediment fractions (Nsed), or Nsed was outside allowable limits.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not determine a valid number of sediment fractions from the sediment control file, or the number was outside the allowable range. The simulation will attempt to continue with a minimum of one sediment fraction.


Suggestions
Check the sediment control file for errors in the sediment fraction configuration. The number of sediment fractions must be less than 10.

title: Message 10055
text:
End time MUST be specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The End Time == command was not found in the main fvc file, or any include files or event files. TUFLOW FV requires an explicit end time in all simulations.


Suggestions
Add an End Time == command to the model fvc file with the intended simulation end time.

title: Message 10057
text:
Error in water quality model: \<wq_error\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred in the water quality model during initialisation. The specific error message from the water quality model is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the water quality control file and and water quality log file for further information.

title: Message 10059
text:
Number of output statements is greater than maximum allowed, \<max_outputs\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during control file processing when the number of Output blocks exceeds the maximum allowed, shown as <max_outputs> in the message text.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of Output blocks in the model control file to within the stated limit.

title: Message 10061
text:
Polygon file used for this BC/Structure, ignoring any READ GIS SA/ZN polygons



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This warning is raised during control file processing when a Polygon File is specified directly for a boundary condition or structure. The directly specified polygon file takes precedence, and any polygons defined via Read GIS SA or Read GIS ZN are ignored for that BC or structure.


Suggestions
No action is required if the polygon file is intentional. To use Read GIS SA or Read GIS ZN polygons for this BC or structure instead, remove the Polygon File specification.

title: Message 10063
text:
TPC outputs disabled as GIS integration has not been enabled for this model.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TPC output types require GIS integration to be enabled. This warning is raised when TPC outputs are requested but the model has not been initialised with GIS integration enabled. The TPC outputs are disabled for the current simulation.


Suggestions
To enable GIS integration, initialise the model following the model initialisation procedure outlined in the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10065
text:
TUFLOW WQ Module requires simulation of salinity. Exiting



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the water quality module is selected but salinity simulation is not enabled in the model control file. The WQ module requires salinity to be active.


Suggestions
Add Include Salinity == 1,  to the model control file, where <coupling> is 1 to couple salinity to density or 0 to decouple.

title: Message 10067
text:
This is a 3D simulation and a constant viscosity/diffusivity vertical mixing model is being used. Should a more advanced mixing model have been specified?



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A constant viscosity and diffusivity vertical mixing model is being used in a 3D simulation. A turbulence closure model may produce more physically accurate results for simulations where vertical mixing is important.


Suggestions
If using a constant mixing model is intentional no action is required. Otherwise review the vertical mixing model specification in the control file and consider specifying a turbulence closure model.

title: Message 10069
text:
Wet depth is less than dry depth. Momentum will never be switched off



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Cell Wet/Dry Depths command sets a dry depth (hdry) as the first argument and a wet depth (hwet) as the second argument in meters or feet. Cells with depth below hwet have their momentum switched off. Cells below hdry are fully deactivated. The intended configuration is that hdry is smaller than hwet, so there is a shallow buffer zone where cells remain active but carry no momentum.
When hwet is not larger than hdry, this buffer zone does not exist. No cell depth is both above the dry threshold and below the wet threshold, so momentum is never suppressed before a cell goes fully dry. This can lead to non-physical velocities or unstable model behaviour in shallow depths.


Suggestions
Ensure the wet depth is greater than the dry depth in Cell Wet/Dry Depths ==. If unsure, the defaults (hdry = 1e-5 m, hwet = 1e-2 m) are suitable for most models.

title: Message 10071
text:
"Blockage" definition error (>100.0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the blockage value for culvert <culvert_id> exceeds 100. Blockage must be a percentage in the range 0–100.


Suggestions
Check the blockage column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value to a valid percentage.

title: Message 10073
text:
"Ignore" == 1, Culvert data not processed, ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This warning is raised when the Ignore column is set to 1 for culvert <culvert_id>. The culvert entry is skipped and has no effect on the simulation.


Suggestions
No action is required if the culvert is intentionally inactive. To activate the culvert, set the Ignore column to 0 in the culvert input file.

title: Message 10075
text:
"Number_of" definition error (<1.0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the Number_of value for culvert <culvert_id> is less than 1. The number of culvert barrels must be at least 1.


Suggestions
Check the Number_of column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value.

title: Message 10077
text:
"n_or_n_F" definition error (<=0.0), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the n_or_n_F value for culvert <culvert_id> is zero or negative. This column holds Manning’s ‘n’ value.


Suggestions
Check the n_or_n_F column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and correct the value.

title: Message 10079
text:
Could not find specified ID in culvert file, ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the culvert ID specified in the model control file cannot be matched to any row in the culvert input file.


Suggestions
Check that culvert <culvert_id> exists in the culvert input file and that the ID column value matches exactly what is specified in the control file.

title: Message 10081
text:
Culvert upstream invert is less than ground elevation, ID \<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV checks each culvert’s invert elevations against the bed elevation of the mesh cells in the culvert’s upstream connection (nodestring or zone) during model initialisation. This message is raised when the upstream invert elevation is lower than the minimum bed elevation in those cells, meaning the culvert opening sits below the ground surface as represented in the mesh.
The severity is controlled by the Culvert Invert Check == command. It is raised as an error by default and can be downgraded to a warning by setting Culvert Invert Check == WARNING.


Suggestions
Check the upstream invert elevation specified for the culvert in the culvert definition file and compare it against the bed elevation of the mesh at the upstream connection. The invert elevation should be at or above the ground surface as defined by the mesh bathymetry.
If the discrepancy is small and physically reasonable (for example, where the mesh resolution means bed elevations are coarser than the culvert geometry), set Culvert Invert Check == WARNING in the control file to allow the simulation to proceed with a warning rather than an error.

title: Message 10083
text:
Irregular "Type" currently not supported (Type=4,6), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when culvert <culvert_id> has Type set to 4 or 6. Irregular cross-section types (Type=4 and Type=6) are not currently supported.


Suggestions
Use a supported culvert type (1, 2, 3, or 5) for culvert <culvert_id>. Contact support@tuflow.com if irregular cross-section support is required.

title: Message 10085
text:
Unrecognised "Type" (1<=val<=6), ID\<culvert_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during culvert initialisation when the Type value for culvert <culvert_id> is outside the valid range of 1 to 6.


Suggestions
Check the Type column in the culvert input file for culvert <culvert_id> and set it to a valid culvert type. Refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual for a description of the supported culvert types.

title: Message 10087
text:
Error deconstructing water quality model: \<wq_error\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during simulation shutdown when the water quality model fails to clean up model files and file memory. The error detail from the WQ module is shown as <wq_error> in the message text.


Suggestions
Review the water quality model configuration and any preceding WQ-related messages in the log file and water quality log file. This issue should not typically occur, so if the cause is not clear please contact support@tuflow.com for assistance.

title: Message 10089
text:
NaN value detected in cell \<2d_cell_id\>, conserved variable \<conserved_variable\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised during the simulation when a NaN (not-a-number) value is detected in a conserved variable at the specified 2D cell. The <conserved_variable> index is numbered sequentially: water depth (1), x-momentum (2), y-momentum (3), then any active scalar constituents in the order they are included — salinity, temperature, tracers (1…N), suspended sediment fractions (1…N), water quality constituents (1…N). The exact index for any scalar depends on which constituents are active in the simulation.


Suggestions
A NaN (not-a-number) value typically indicates a model instability has occured. Review the model setup around cell <2d_cell_id>, its location should be reported in the GIS messages layer.
Identify which conserved variable <conserved_variable> is NaN. Review the map output for this variable leading up the time of the error for any unusual behaviour.
There are a range of potential causes for a model going unstable but common issues are as follows.

The model mesh quality in the region surrounding the offending <2d_cell_id> can be improved, or there are sharp gradients in topogrography or bathymetry in this area that could be better resolved by the mesh
Boundary conditions, initial conditions, or edited restart files may not be consistent with expected model configuration, or include erroneous or non-physical values. The user should review each of these to ensure they are suitable
The computational timestep for the model may need to be reduced. Refer to the TUFLOW FV User Manual for guidance on timestep selection and stability criteria
The sediment update dt for sediment transport and morphological coupling may be too high
Water quality processes may be incorrectly configured

While the error will be reported at the first cell where NaN is detected, the root cause may originate from a nearby cell. To track where instability begins, add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to the error. See ERROR 10097 for an example output block.

title: Message 10091
text:
Simulation has run beyond transport file limits



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The simulation has advanced beyond the end of the time records in the transport file. The transport file must cover the full simulation period for transport boundary conditions to remain synchronised.


Suggestions
Check that the transport file covers the full simulation period. If the simulation end time has been extended beyond the period covered by the transport file it will need to be regenerated.

title: Message 10093
text:
Velocity has exceeded stability limit \<velocity_stability_limit\> (m/s or ft/s) at 2D cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The velocity at the cell shown has exceeded the configured stability limit during the simulation. This may indicate numerical instability which has caused the solution to diverge at this location. The velocity stability limit is the second argument set using Stability Limits ==.


Suggestions
The stability limits can be adjusted using the Stability Limits == command in the model control file. Ensure that the specified velocity limit argument reflects the expected flow conditions being investigated. A velocity limit of 10 m/s is commonly used.
The simulation time at which the error occurs may help to diagnose the issue. If the error occurs early in the simulation or at initialisation, it is likely a model configuration, initial condition or boundary condition mismatch. If the error occurs later during the simulation and the model configuration appears correct, the region surrounding the offending 2d cell(s) warrants further investigation for instabilities.
For model instability, review the model setup in the vicinity of the cell shown in the GIS messages output file. Common causes include a timestep that is too large for the mesh resolution, poor mesh quality near the affected cell and extreme or incorrectly specified boundary conditions.
While the error will be reported at the first cell that exceeds the specified stability limit, the root case may originate from a different cell, typically close by. To track where velocity divergence begins, it may be useful to add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to when the error occurs. For example, if the model crashes at 02/12/2008 21:15:36:
Output == NetCDF 
    Suffix == CHK                             ! For checking
    Output Parameters == h, v                 ! Water level, velocity
    Start Output == 02/12/2008 21:15:00       ! Time close to the error occurrence
    Final Output == 02/12/2008 21:17:00       ! Time immediately after the crash, mainly for safety so the model cannot continue writing high temporal resolution output AND FILL UP RESULT STORAGE. BE CAREFUL!!!!
    Output Interval == 1                      ! (s) High temporal resolution output to help track initial cell where instability starts and propagation
End Output
This block writes water level and velocity at 1 second intervals (0 will use the model timestep if higher temporal resolution is required) in a narrow window around the error. Stepping through the output in time allows identification of the initial cell where instability begins and its propagation path.
The command Write Restart At Time == can also be useful to start a follow-up run close to the time of the error.

title: Message 10095
text:
Warning: Geometry netCDF file records mesh geometry in metric units



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
When geometry netCDF echoing is enabled the geometry file is always written in metric units regardless of the model unit system. This warning is issued when the model is running in imperial units.


Suggestions
If the geometry netCDF file is used in post-processing ensure the appropriate unit conversion is applied. Geometry netCDF echoing is enabled by the Echo Geometry == 1 or Echo Geometry NetCDF == 1 commands in the model control file.

title: Message 10097
text:
Water surface has exceeded stability limit \<water_surface_stability_limit\> (mRL or ftRL) at 2D cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The water surface elevation at a 2D mesh cell has exceeded the upper stability limit set by Stability Limits ==. The water surface stability limit is the first argument of Stability Limits ==. TUFLOW FV checks solution bounds after applying initial conditions and periodically during the simulation.


Suggestions
The stability limits can be adjusted using the Stability Limits == command. The first argument is the upper bound for water surface elevation in mRL (or ftRL). Ensure it is set well above the maximum expected water level and topography/bathymetry values in the domain. Setting a water level stability limit lower than the maximum topographic/bathymetric Zb in the model domain is a common cause of this error.
The simulation time at which the error occurs may help to diagnose the issue. If the error occurs early in the simulation or at initialisation, it is likely a model configuration, initial condition or boundary condition mismatch. If the error occurs later during the simulation and the model configuration appears correct, the region surrounding the offending 2D cell warrants further investigation for instabilities.
If the error occurs at initialisation, check the initial condition data for water surface values that exceed the configured limit. The 2d cell ID in the message can be matched to a point in the GIS messages output file.
For model instability, review the model setup in the vicinity of the cell shown in the GIS messages output file. Common causes include a timestep that is too large for the mesh resolution, poor mesh quality near the affected cell and extreme or incorrectly specified boundary conditions.
While the error will be reported at the first cell that exceeds the specified stability limit the root case may originate from a different cell, typically close by. To track where instability begins it may be useful to add a secondary output block with high temporal resolution at a time just prior to when the error occurs. For example, if the model crashes at 02/12/2008 21:15:36:
Output == NetCDF 
    Suffix == CHK                             ! For checking
    Output Parameters == h, v                 ! Water level, velocity
    Start Output == 02/12/2008 21:15:00       ! Time close to the error occurrence
    Final Output == 02/12/2008 21:17:00       ! Time immediately after the crash, mainly for safety so the model cannot continue writing high temporal resolution output AND FILL UP RESULT STORAGE. BE CAREFUL!!!!
    Output Interval == 1                      ! (s) High temporal resolution output to help track initial cell where instability starts and propagation
End Output
This block writes water level and velocity at 1 second intervals (0 will use the model timestep if higher temporal resolution is required) in a narrow window around the error. Stepping through the output in time allows identification of the initial cell where instability begins and its propagation path.
The command Write Restart At Time == can also be useful to start a follow-up run close to the time of the error.

title: Message 10099
text:
invalid auto-termination flag



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error is raised when the internal auto-termination flag for the Auto Terminate == command has an unexpected value. This is an internal consistency error and should not occur under normal circumstances.


Suggestions
Check the Auto Terminate == specification. If the command is correctly configured and the error persists, contact support@tuflow.com.

title: Message 10101
text:
Nodes \<node_id\> and \<duplicate_node_id\> are duplicates!



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two mesh nodes are at the same or nearly identical coordinates resulting in a mesh face with zero length. This indicates a meshing error.


Suggestions
Open the mesh and remove or merge the duplicate nodes. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the duplicated nodes. Export the corrected mesh before running the simulation again.

title: Message 10103
text:
error echoing internal face geometry \<file_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A write error occurred while echoing internal face geometry to the diagnostic output file with the reported file ID.


Suggestions
Check that the output directory exists, is writable, and has sufficient disk space.

title: Message 10105
text:
one or more subroutine arguments not constructed



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more required data structures had not been constructed before a mesh processing routine was called. This is an internal software issue and should not occur under normal circumstances.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please send through the log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10107
text:
Error in file: \<file_name\>, Line \<line_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A data error was found in the specified TIN file at the reported line. This is raised when a vertex has a zero x or y coordinate, which indicates an invalid or uninitialised entry.


Suggestions
Open the TIN file and check the reported line for zero or missing vertex coordinates.

title: Message 10109
text:
Maximum number of open files exceeded



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV has reached its internal limit of 100 simultaneously open files.


Suggestions
Check whether the model has an unusually large number of output files configured. Reducing the number of concurrent output files or combining outputs may resolve the issue.

title: Message 10111
text:
Unsupported Zpts Grid file format



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Zpts grid file read using Read GRID Zpts has an extension that is not supported. Supported formats are asc and flt.


Suggestions
Convert the grid file to asc or flt format in a GIS or grid editing software and update the file path in the control file.

title: Message 10113
text:
maximum number of characters allowed per line in csv file is \<max_characters\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A line in the csv file has reached or exceeded the maximum supported length of 10,000 characters. Data beyond this limit will be truncated.


Suggestions
Check the csv file for unexpectedly long lines and shorten them. This may indicate extra whitespace, spurious content, or an incorrectly formatted file.

title: Message 10115
text:
Bed layer (SIGMA=0.0) should not be explicitly specified in layer file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The file referenced by the Layer Face File command contains a sigma value of 0.0, which corresponds to the bed layer. TUFLOW FV adds the bed layer (SIGMA=0) automatically and it must not be included in the layer file.


Suggestions
Remove the SIGMA=0.0 entry from the Layer Face File. Only interior sigma layer boundaries between 0 and 1 (exclusive) should be specified.

title: Message 10117
text:
Cartesian model specified with coordinates within range [-360.,360.], [-90.,90.]. Check if spherical coordinates should be specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The model is set to use a Cartesian coordinate system, but all mesh node coordinates fall within the range typical of geographic (longitude/latitude) coordinates (x within ±360°, y within ±90°).
