This may indicate that the coordinate system setting in the control file does not match the coordinate system of the mesh.


Suggestions
Check whether the mesh was created using geographic coordinates (longitude/latitude). If so, use Spherical == 1 to the control file.
If the model is correctly using a Cartesian coordinate system and the node coordinates happen to fall within the geographic coordinate range, this warning can be ignored.

title: Message 10119
text:
Duplicate Polygon/Point id: \<point_label\> found in \<file_name\> files.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two or more GIS objects within the same GIS layer share the same ID. Duplicate IDs within a layer are not permitted as they cause ambiguous boundary condition assignment.


Suggestions
Open the reported GIS layer and ensure each polygon or point has a unique ID. Rename any duplicates and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10121
text:
Duplicated nodestring ID in 2dm file: \<nodestring_id_2dm_file\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The reported nodestring ID appears more than once in the 2dm file. Nodestring IDs must be unique within the 2dm file.


Suggestions
Open the 2dm file and check the NS entries for the reported ID. Assign a unique ID to each nodestring.

title: Message 10123
text:
Elevation less than -9999. encountered at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A cell with a bed elevation below −9999 m was detected after applying elevation data to the mesh. Values in this range are almost certainly NoData or null values from a bathymetry or DEM dataset that have been incorrectly applied to the mesh rather than masked.


Suggestions
Review the bathymetry and DEM source files for NoData regions. Ensure the NoData value is correctly specified in the source data so that cells without valid elevation data are not assigned unrealistic values.
Use the GIS messages output file to identify the affected cells and inspect the source data in those areas.

title: Message 10125
text:
Error echoing spatial geometry log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A write error occurred while initialising, updating, or closing the spatial geometry log file (_geo.csv).


Suggestions
Check that the output log directory exists (set via the Log Dir == command), is writable, and has sufficient disk space.

title: Message 10127
text:
Fixed Grid Gridsize has not been specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A fixed grid mesh was requested but no grid size was provided. The Grid Size == keyword is required when using a fixed grid mesh.


Suggestions
Add Grid Size ==   to the control file to specify the overall fixed grid dimensions.

title: Message 10129
text:
Found \<2d_cell_count\> cell-centroids along polyline



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No mesh cell centroids were found along the elevation polyline. The polyline does not intersect any mesh cells and will not contribute to the bed elevation.


Suggestions
Check that the elevation polyline overlaps the mesh and is in the correct coordinate projection.

title: Message 10131
text:
Found \<2d_cell_count\> cell-vertexes in polygon



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No mesh node vertices were found inside the elevation polygon. The polygon does not overlap any mesh nodes and will not contribute to the bed elevation.


Suggestions
Check that the elevation polygon overlaps the mesh and is in the correct coordinate projection. Ensure the polygon covers at least one mesh node vertex.

title: Message 10133
text:
Inactive material block specification, ID \<material_id\> is not supported with external material layers.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A material ID block specified with Inactive == matches a material ID found in a 2d_mat GIS material layer. Deactivating specific material IDs is not supported when materials are assigned from an external GIS layer.


Suggestions
Remove the Inactive == entry for the reported material ID, or assign the material ID directly to the model mesh during mesh generation.

title: Message 10135
text:
Linear elements only expected



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The 2dm mesh file contains higher-order element types (E6T, E8Q, or E9Q). TUFLOW FV only supports linear elements: 3-node triangles (E3T) and 4-node quadrilaterals (E4Q).


Suggestions
Ensure the mesh generator is configured to generate linear meshes. Regenerate the mesh using only linear elements and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10137
text:
No points found in elevation polygon!



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No points were found in the elevation polygon CSV file matching the specified polygon ID. The optional polygon ID is the third comma separated argument to Cell Elevation Polygon File ==.


Suggestions
Check that the ID column in the csv file contains the specified polygon ID.

title: Message 10139
text:
No points found in material polygon!



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
No polygon points were found for a material ID when processing the csv file specified via Material Polygon File ==. The csv must have X, Y, and ID columns. The affected material ID is skipped and will not be applied to the mesh.


Suggestions
Check the Material Polygon File == csv for the reported material ID and verify that the polygon data is complete and the ID values are integers.
The Material Polygon File == csv file must have the following columns: X, Y, and ID. The ID column must contain integer values. The X and Y columns must contain valid coordinates for the polygon points.
The Material Polygon File == command is depreciated and it is recommended to use Read GIS Mat with GIS integration.

title: Message 10141
text:
Number of breakline points exceeds maximum



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total number of breakline points across all breakline GIS layers exceeds the internal limit of 500,000 points.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of breakline points by simplifying or splitting the breakline GIS data, or by removing breaklines that are not needed for the current simulation.

title: Message 10143
text:
Number of requested nodestrings is greater than upper limit (\<max_nodestrings\>).



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total number of nodestrings in the mesh exceeds the internal limit of 500. This is the combined number of nodestrings specified in the .2dm mesh file and via 2d_ns GIS layers.


Suggestions
Where possible, reduce the number of nodestrings in the mesh by simplifying or splitting the nodestring GIS data, or by removing nodestrings that are not needed for the current simulation. If the number of nodestrings cannot be reduced, contact support@tuflow.com to discuss options for increasing the internal limit.

title: Message 10145
text:
Out-of-range longitude [-360.,360.] encountered at node:\<node_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A mesh node has a longitude coordinate outside the valid range of −360° to 360°. This indicates the mesh coordinates are either in the wrong projection or the model is incorrectly configured to use spherical coordinates.


Suggestions
Check that the mesh coordinates are in geographic (latitude/longitude) decimal degrees. If the mesh is in a projected coordinate system set the model to use Cartesian coordinates in the control file. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the out-of-range node.

title: Message 10147
text:
SIGMA column must be monotonically decreasing



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sigma layer values in the csv file specified by Layer Face File == are not monotonically decreasing. This check applies when Vertical Mesh Type == SIGMA. Sigma values must be listed from the highest value (near the surface) to the lowest (near the bed), with each value strictly less than the previous. Importantly the surface value of 1.0 or the bed 0.0 should not be included in the csv file, as these are automatically applied by TUFLOW FV.


Suggestions
Check the SIGMA column in the layer file and reorder the values so they are strictly decreasing from top to bottom.

title: Message 10149
text:
Some nodestrings have failed to be built. See previous ERROR messages.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more nodestrings could not be built during initialisation. This is a summary message. The specific failures are reported by the preceding ERROR messages.


Suggestions
Review the preceding WARNING 10389 messages for details on which nodestrings failed and why. Correct the issues identified in the GIS layer or control file and run the simulation again.
This error can occur when using the boundary fitting BD flag in the 2d_ns layer. Check that internal nodestrings are not using the BD flag.
If specifying an internal or boundary nodestring try inserting additional vertices along the nodestring to assist the nodestring path algorithm in finding the cell face path.

title: Message 10151
text:
Unexpected id encountered. Cell id = \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
When reading a Cell Elevation File in ID format, TUFLOW FV could not find a mesh cell matching the ID specified in the file. Cells with unrecognised IDs are skipped and will not have their bed elevation updated. This warning can appear many times per simulation if a large number of IDs in the file do not match the current mesh.


Suggestions
Check that the Cell Elevation File was generated from the same mesh currently being used. If the mesh has been regenerated or refined since the elevation file was created, cell IDs may have changed and the file will need to be regenerated.
If only a small number of IDs are unrecognised, check the ID column of the Cell Elevation File for values that fall outside the valid range of mesh cell IDs.

title: Message 10153
text:
Z column must be monotonically decreasing



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
When reading the layer face elevation file for a z-coordinate 3D model, the Z column values must be listed in monotonically decreasing order from the highest elevation to the lowest. This error is raised when that ordering condition is not met.


Suggestions
Check the layer face file specified by Layer Face File == and ensure the Z column values decrease from top to bottom with no repeated values or values that increase between rows.

title: Message 10155
text:
ZLine Point not snapped to start of line



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The first vertex of the ZLine breakline has no elevation point snapped to it. When elevation points are used with a breakline the first and last vertices of the line must each have an elevation point snapped to them.


Suggestions
Add an elevation point snapped to the first vertex of the ZLine. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the unsnapped start vertex.

title: Message 10157
text:
overlapping elements detected: \<mesh_2dm_cell_ids\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two or more mesh cells share the same pair of vertices more than twice, indicating that the cells geometrically overlap. The cell IDs of the overlapping elements are listed in the message.


Suggestions
Open the mesh and inspect the reported cell IDs for overlapping geometry. Correct the mesh by removing or separating the overlapping elements and rerun the simulation.
This issue can occur if the mesh has been manually edited and mesh error have been introduced.

title: Message 10159
text:
Duplicated GIS point id \<point_id\>, in layer \<2d_sa_layer\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two points in the same GIS layer share the same ID. Point IDs must be unique.


Suggestions
Open the named GIS layer and assign a unique ID to each point. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the duplicated point.

title: Message 10161
text:
Duplicated nodestring id \<nodestring_id\>, in layer \<2d_ns_layer\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two nodestrings in the same GIS layer share the same ID. Nodestring IDs must be unique within a layer.


Suggestions
Open the named GIS layer and assign a unique ID to each nodestring. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the duplicated nodestring.

title: Message 10163
text:
GIS PO points should have either 3 or 5 attributes



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The GIS point output (PO) layer does not have the expected number of attribute columns. TUFLOW FV requires a PO GIS layer to have either 3 or 5 attributes. The 3 attribute format is Type, ID and Comment. The 5 attribute format adds Layer Min and Layer Max for 3D output with a vertical range.


Suggestions
Check the GIS PO layer schema and correct it to match one of the supported formats. It is recommended to generate 3d_po template layers via the Write Emtpy GIS Files == command. Refer to the model initalisation section of the TUFLOW FV User Manual.

title: Message 10165
text:
Less than required 2 2d_ns attributes



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The 2d_ns GIS layer has fewer than the required 2 attribute columns. TUFLOW FV requires at least an ID and a Flags attribute in the nodestring layer.


Suggestions
This can commonly occur if the 2d_ns GIS layer was created manually. Check the schema of the 2d_ns GIS layer and ensure it has at least 2 attributes. It is recommended to generate template layers using Write Empty GIS Files == using TUFLOW FV’s GIS integration, which will create the required attributes automatically. Refer to the model initialisation section of the TUFLOW FV User Manual for more information.

title: Message 10167
text:
Material \<material_id\> within GIS layer not specified in control file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A material ID found in the GIS materials layer (2d_mat) is not defined in any material block in the control file. Every material ID assigned in the GIS layer must have a corresponding material specification in the control file.


Suggestions
Check the GIS materials layer for the reported material ID and add a corresponding Material ==  block to the control file. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the unrecognised polygon.

title: Message 10169
text:
Object in GIS polygon is not a region or a point, skipping.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An object in the SA or ZN GIS layer has an unrecognised or unsupported geometry type that cannot be read. The object is skipped. The layer expects only polygon (region) or point objects.


Suggestions
Open the SA or ZN GIS layer and check for objects with unsupported geometry types such as lines, text, or multipoint objects. Remove them and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10171
text:
Object in nodestring gis file is not a line or polyline, skipping.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An object in the 2d_ns GIS nodestring layer has an unrecognised or unsupported geometry type that cannot be read. The object is skipped. The layer expects only line or polyline objects.


Suggestions
Open the 2d_ns GIS layer and check for objects with unsupported geometry types such as null shapes, points, text, or multipoint objects. Remove them and rerun the simulation.

title: Message 10173
text:
UNSUPPORTED FILE FORMAT FOR MATERIALS: \<material_file\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The materials file format is not supported. Supported formats for Read GIS Mat == are shp and mif.


Suggestions
Check the file extension of the materials file and use a supported format.

title: Message 10175
text:
Duplicate BC event source found: \<bc_event_text\> | \<bc_event_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The same BC event source variable name has been defined more than once within a Define Event block. Each variable name must be unique within an event definition.


Suggestions
Check the Define Event block(s) in the control file for duplicate BC Event Source == entries and remove the duplicate.

title: Message 10177
text:
Exceeded maximum number of allowed user variables (\<max_user_variables\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of user variables defined via Set Variable == exceeds the internal limit of 100.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of Set Variable == entries.

title: Message 10179
text:
Variable defined more than once: \<max_user_variable_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The same user variable name has been defined more than once via Set Variable ==. Each variable name must be unique.


Suggestions
Check the control file for duplicate Set Variable == entries with the reported name and remove the duplicate.

title: Message 10181
text:
NaN detected in grid horizontal coordinates



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised after reading the x and y coordinate variables from a netCDF grid file when one or more values are NaN. This indicates the coordinate data in the file is corrupt or incomplete.


Suggestions
Check the netCDF grid file for missing or invalid values in the x and y coordinate variables. Re-export or reprocess the file to ensure all horizontal coordinate values are finite.

title: Message 10183
text:
Specified TIN is not coincident with model mesh.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a TIN specified for bed elevation assignment (via Cell Elevation TIN == or Read TIN Zpts ==) does not overlap with any cell in the model mesh. The TIN to mesh mapping produced zero coincident cells, so no elevations can be assigned.


Suggestions
Check that the TIN file covers the intended area of the model mesh and that both are in the same coordinate system.

title: Message 10185
text:
Specified grid is not coincident with scatter point set.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a grid definition is being mapped against a set of scatter points and none of those points fall within the grid extent. No interpolated values can be assigned from this grid to the scatter point set.


Suggestions
Check that the grid coordinate system and extents are consistent with the scatter point locations. If the grid is specified inline via Grid Definition ==, verify the origin (x0, y0), rotation angle, cell counts (mx, my), and cell sizes (dx, dy). If specified via a netCDF file using Grid Definition File ==, verify the coordinate variables in that file.

title: Message 10187
text:
Partial TIN coverage: \<2d_cell_count\> model cells (\<perc_total_2d_cells\> %) fall within TIN extent.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Not all model domain mesh cells fall within the extent of the TIN. Cells outside the TIN will not receive elevation data from this source.


Suggestions
Check that the TIN extent covers the full model domain. If partial coverage is intentional no action is required. If the coverage gap is unexpected check that the TIN projection and extent match the model domain.

title: Message 10189
text:
Partial grid coverage: \<2d_node_count\> model nodes (\<perc_total_2d_nodes\> %) fall within grid extent.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Not all model domain mesh nodes fall within the extent of the input grid. Nodes outside the grid extent will not receive data from this grid source.


Suggestions
Check that the grid extent covers the full model domain. If partial coverage is intentional no action is required. If the coverage gap is unexpected check that the grid file projection and extent match the model domain.

title: Message 10191
text:
Partial grid coverage: \<number_scatter_points\> scatter points (\<perc_total_scatter_points\> %) fall within grid extent.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Not all scatter points fall within the extent of the specified grid. Scatter points outside the grid extent will not receive interpolated values from this grid source.


Suggestions
Check that the grid extent covers the full set of scatter points. If partial coverage is intentional no action is required. If the gap is unexpected, verify that the grid coordinate system and extents match the scatter point locations.

title: Message 10193
text:
NaN detected in OGCM initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when initialising from an OGCM boundary condition (via Initial Condition OGCM) and NaN values remain in the state array after interpolating the OGCM grid data onto the mesh and attempting to fill any gaps. This indicates the OGCM grid data does not adequately cover the model domain.


Suggestions
Check that the OGCM boundary condition grid covers the full model domain. If there are gaps at the domain edges, consider extending the OGCM grid or adjusting the model domain extents.
TUFLOW FV will attempt to fill any gaps in the OGCM data by interpolating from the nearest valid values. If this is not possible, NaN values will remain in the state array and this error will be raised.

title: Message 10195
text:
NaN detected in global scalar profile initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when applying a global scalar vertical profile initial condition (via Initial Scalar Profile ==) and NaN values remain in the scalar fields after interpolating the profile onto the 3D mesh.


Suggestions
Open the csv profile file and check for missing or invalid values in any of the scalar columns (e.g. SAL, TEMP). All rows must have valid numeric entries.

title: Message 10197
text:
NaN detected in global temperature initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the global temperature initial condition value (specified via Initial Temperature ==) is NaN when applied. This can occur if the value in the control file could not be parsed as a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the Initial Temperature == line in the control file and ensure a valid numeric value is specified.

title: Message 10199
text:
NaN detected in global wq concentration initial conditions



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the global water quality concentration initial condition value (specified via Initial WQ Concentration ==) is NaN when applied. This can occur if the value in the control file could not be parsed as a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the Initial WQ Concentration == line in the control file and ensure a valid numeric value is specified for each water quality constituent being simulated.

title: Message 10201
text:
Could not find directory: \<directory\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a required output or check directory does not exist and automatic directory creation is not enabled. The missing directory path is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Create the directory before running the model, or check the path specified via Log Dir ==, Output Dir == or Write Check Files == for typos. Ensure the parent directory exists and has write permissions for the user executing the simulation.
Directory creation is enabled by default, so this error typically only occurs when MkDir == 0 has been set. If directories are expected to be created automatically, check that MkDir == 0 has not been specified.

title: Message 10203
text:
Error encountered closing file unit \<file_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a file close operation returns a non-zero status for a file unit. The file unit number is reported in the message.


Suggestions
This is typically caused by a file system issue. Check available disk space and ensure the output directory remains accessible throughout the simulation.
Typically the file unit number can be traced by an earlier message reporting the file name and unit number when the file was opened. This can be used to help identify the file that failed to close. If storage or directory access issues appears unlikely, check the file for corruption or other issues that may have prevented it from being closed successfully.

title: Message 10205
text:
Error reading csv file \<file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a csv file cannot be read or returns no data. This applies to csv files used for polyline nodestrings and curtain output definitions. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the file exists at the specified path, is a valid csv, and contains the required column headers and data.

title: Message 10207
text:
Error reading restart file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when reading a binary restart file fails after the file has been opened successfully. This applies to the hydrodynamic (.rst), turbulence (_turb.rst), sediment (_bed.rst) and particle tracking restart files (_ptm.rst).


Suggestions
Check that the restart file is not corrupt or truncated. If the restart file was generated by a different model version or configuration it may be incompatible. If the restart has been manually edited, check the file has not been corrupted or the dimensions altered from the original.
Check that the correct restart file is being read for the required command. A common error is to attempt to read a restart file with the wrong command. The compatible restart file for each command is as follows.

The Restart File == command in the .fvc will read a restart file generated by the hydrodynamic engine, which have a .rst extension with no additional file suffix. If a _turb.rst with the same name exists in the same directory it will be read automatically. For example Restart File == log/my_run_001.rst will read log/my_run_001.rst and log/my_run_001_turb.rst if it exists.
The sediment control file Bed Restart File == command should be used to read the _bed.rst file
The particle tracking control file Particle Restart File == command should be used to read the _ptm.rst file.

title: Message 10209
text:
Log directory does not exist: \<log_directory\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the log directory specified via Log Dir == does not exist and MkDir == 0 has been set to disable automatic directory creation.


Suggestions
Create the log directory before running the model, or remove MkDir == 0 to allow TUFLOW FV to create it automatically.
Directory creation is enabled by default, so this error typically only occurs when MkDir == 0 has been set. If directories are expected to be created automatically, check that MkDir == 0 has not been specified.
Check that the user executing the simulation has write permissions for the parent directory of the log directory.

title: Message 10211
text:
Restart file time validation error



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The timestamp recorded in the restart file is earlier than the simulation start time (as set via Start Time ==). This is not permitted.


Suggestions
Check that the correct restart file is specified in the control file. Alternatively set Use Restart File Time == 0 in the control file to skip the time validation and continue from the simulation start time rather than the restart file time.

title: Message 10213
text:
Unable to open restart file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
When reading a restart file, TUFLOW FV also attempts to read companion restart files for optional model components such as turbulence state (_turb.rst) and ice state (_ice.rst). This warning is raised when a companion restart file cannot be opened. The simulation continues with default initial conditions for the affected component.


Suggestions
This warning is expected when using a restart file from a simulation that did not include the same model components. For example, using a restart from a simulation run without a turbulence closure scheme to initialise a model that includes one. In this case the warning can be ignored.
If the companion restart file is expected to exist, check that the file path is correct and that the file has not been moved or deleted.

title: Message 10215
text:
error closing log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when closing the log file at the end of the simulation fails.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available and that the log directory remains writable. If the log file was deleted or moved during the simulation this error may also occur.

title: Message 10217
text:
error opening structural log file, \<structure_logging_file\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the structure logging file (.slf) cannot be opened for writing. Structure logging is enabled via Structure Logging == 1. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the log directory exists and is writable. Verify that no other process has the file open and that the path does not contain invalid characters. Ensure the user running the simulation has write permission to the log directory. If Log Dir == has been specified, verify the path is correct.

title: Message 10219
text:
error reading file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when an input file cannot be read. This occurs when the file is empty or when a low-level I/O error prevents the first line from being read successfully.


Suggestions
Check that the file is not empty and has not been truncated. Verify that the file can be opened normally outside of TUFLOW FV. If the file appears intact, check that the storage location is accessible and the file system is healthy.

title: Message 10221
text:
error writing cfl information \<cfl_file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing the CFL statistics csv file fails. CFL statistics output is enabled via Output CFL Stats == 1 and writes cell face timestep constraint data to a csv file in the log directory.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the log directory and that the directory remains writable during the simulation. Make sure the file is not open in another application capablle of locking the file.

title: Message 10223
text:
error writing face debug info



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing face debug output to a binary debug snapshot file fails. Face debug output is used occasionally by the TUFLOW FV development team to diagnose issues and is not intended for general use. The file name is reported in the message.


Suggestions
If you see this error contact support@tuflow.com for further assistance.

title: Message 10225
text:
error writing to file unit\<file_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing to an output file fails during the simulation. The file unit number is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the output directory and that the directory remains writable during the simulation.
The file name associated with the file unit number should be reported close to the file_id in the log file. Check that the file is not open in another application capable of locking the file and that the filesize is reasonable.

title: Message 10227
text:
error writing to structure log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when writing to the structure logging file (.slf) fails. Structure logging is enabled via Structure Logging == ON.


Suggestions
Check that sufficient disk space is available in the log directory and that the .slf file has not been deleted or made read only while the simulation is running.

title: Message 10229
text:
incompatible number of layer faces in turbulence restart file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when the number of vertical layer faces in the turbulence restart file (_turb.rst) does not match the current model’s layer configuration. The turbulence restart cannot be applied to a mesh with a different number of vertical layers.


Suggestions
Ensure the restart file was generated by a simulation using the same vertical layer configuration. If the layer scheme has changed, rerun the model to generate a new turbulence restart file.

title: Message 10231
text:
rewind file failed



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when rewinding an input file back to the beginning fails during model initialisation.


Suggestions
This is typically caused by a file system issue. Check that the input file is accessible and that the storage location is functioning correctly. Verify that the file has not been modified or moved since the simulation started.

title: Message 10233
text:
Requested TUFLOW FV engine license not found.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a license cannot be accessed during model license checks. A licence dongle may not be present, the dongle may not hold the required product code, the licence may have expired or there are no available licences. If using a network licence, the licence server may not be accessible or correctly configured.


Suggestions
Refer to the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for further information on licensing and dongle requirements. If the issue persists, Generate a CM Dust File and send both the CM Dust file and TUFLOW FV log file through to support@tuflow.com. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10235
text:
Requested threads licenses not found on available dongle/s.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a license cannot be accessed during model license checks. A licence dongle may not be present, the dongle may not hold the required product code, the licence may have expired or there are no available licences. If using a network licence, the licence server may not be accessible or correctly configured.


Suggestions
Refer to the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for further information on licensing and dongle requirements. If the issue persists, Generate a CM Dust File and send both the CM Dust file and TUFLOW FV log file through to support@tuflow.com. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10237
text:
SORRY - Simulation time using a free licence has exceeded time limit.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a simulation is run using a demo licence (via Demo Model == ON or Tutorial Model == ON) and the permitted simulation time limit has been reached. The simulation cannot continue beyond this limit under a demo licence.


Suggestions
To run longer simulations, a full TUFLOW FV licence is required. Contact support@tuflow.com or visit the TUFLOW FV Licensing Guide for information on obtaining a full licence.

title: Message 10239
text:
Could not make Log directory: \<log_directory\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when TUFLOW FV attempts to create the log directory (specified via Log Dir ==) and the creation fails. The directory path is reported in the message.


Suggestions
Check that the parent directory of the specified log path exists and is writable. On Linux, ensure the user running the simulation has write permission to the parent directory.

title: Message 10241
text:
Very small angle encountered at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A very small interior angle was detected at a cell vertex during mesh preprocessing. Cells with very small interior angles indicate poor mesh quality and can affect numerical accuracy, stability and speed during the simulation.


Suggestions
Review the mesh in the vicinity of the flagged cell. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the problematic vertex which can be used to identify the area requiring attention. Regenerate the mesh with improved element quality.

title: Message 10243
text:
3d output is not supported by SMS binary dat file. Requested output will be 2D depth-averaged.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a 3D output parameter is requested with SMS binary output format. The .dat or .xmdf formats only support 2D depth-averaged data. The output will be written as a depth-averaged result instead.


Suggestions
If 3D layer output is required use the NetCDF output format. If depth-averaged output is acceptable, no action is required.

title: Message 10245
text:
Curtain polyline does not intersect mesh.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when a curtain output polyline (specified via Output Curtain File ==) does not intersect the model mesh. The polyline must cross at least one mesh cell face to produce valid curtain output.


Suggestions
Check that the curtain polyline is correctly positioned within the model domain and uses the same coordinate system as the mesh. Verify the polyline path in a GIS tool against the mesh extents.

title: Message 10247
text:
Duplicate PO id: \<duplicate_po_id\> found in GIS files.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Two or more point output (PO) features in the GIS input file(s) share the same ID. Each PO point must have a unique ID as it is used to identify the output location in the results.


Suggestions
Open the GIS PO file(s) and check for features with duplicate IDs. The GIS messages output file shows the location of the first point with the duplicate ID. Assign a unique ID to each PO point.

title: Message 10249
text:
Error processing output curtain object. Inadmissable cell index.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when constructing a curtain output object and one or more of the interpolated cell indices along the curtain polyline falls outside the valid range of mesh cell IDs. This indicates an internal mapping error between the curtain polyline and the mesh.


Suggestions
Check that the curtain polyline file specified via Output Curtain File == is valid and lies fully within the model domain. If the polyline is correct, contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the TUFLOW FV log file and the curtain polyline file, this will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10251
text:
MMM units system not supported for mass balance outputs. Exiting.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Raised when mass balance output is requested alongside a water quality simulation that uses a units system other than mg/L (milligrams per litre). Mass balance output currently only supports water quality models using mg/L units.


Suggestions
Remove the mass balance output block, or configure the water quality model to use mg/L units. If mass balance output is essential with a different units system, contact support@tuflow.com.

title: Message 10253
text:
Output interval must be higher than the maximum allowed timestep.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The maximum timestep specified by Timestep Limits == is greater than the output interval specified in an output block. TUFLOW FV uses adaptive timestepping, so output cannot be guaranteed at the requested interval if the maximum allowed timestep is larger than it.


Suggestions
Ensure the Output Interval == in each output block is at least as large as the maximum timestep set by Timestep Limits ==. Either increase the output interval or reduce the maximum timestep.

title: Message 10255
text:
Output parameter '\<output_parameter\>' is not supported by the XMDF format.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The output parameter named in the message is not supported by the XMDF format.


Suggestions
Change the output format for the outputparameter to netCDF, or remove the parameter from the XMDF output block.

title: Message 10257
text:
Simulation of internal nutrients not supported for mass balance outputs. Exiting.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The simulation includes internal nutrient water quality variables (internal nitrogen or phosphorus quantities), which are not supported by the mass balance output. Mass balance output cannot be used when the water quality configuration contains internal nutrient parameters.


Suggestions
Remove the MassBalance output block from the control file, or use a water quality configuration that does not include internal nutrient simulation.

title: Message 10259
text:
Unexpected curtain id



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A curtain output block was found without a valid curtain ID. Each Curtain output block requires an Output Curtain File == line specifying both the curtain geometry csv file and a non-zero integer ID corresponding to one of the curtain sections defined in that file.


Suggestions
Add Output Curtain File == ,  to the curtain output block, ensuring <id> is a non-zero integer that matches an ID value in the curtain csv file.

title: Message 10261
text:
Unknown output statistic type, \<output_statistic\> encountered in output request \<output_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The output statistics type named in the message is not recognised for the specified output request. The only valid output statistics types are MAX, MIN and MEAN.


Suggestions
Check the output block identified by the output request number and correct the statistics keyword to one of MAX, MIN or MEAN.

title: Message 10263
text:
Unrecognised variable to convert \<mass_output\> output units: \<mass_output_variable\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An output variable was passed to the unit conversion routine for the named output type that is not recognised. This is an unexpected condition indicating the variable is not supported for that output type.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the simulation log file. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10265
text:
unknown output type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unexpected output type was encountered during output writing. This is an unexpected condition that should not occur under normal operation.


Suggestions
Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the simulation log file. This will help diagnose the issue.

title: Message 10267
text:
Could not find header type NODATA_VALUE or NODATA. Set to -99999 as default



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
When reading an ASC or FLT raster file, TUFLOW FV could not find a NODATA_VALUE or NODATA header entry. The no-data value is set to -99999 as a default and the simulation continues.


Suggestions
Update the input raster to include a non-data value either in a text editor (for ASC only) or the GIS sofware that was used to generate the raster.

title: Message 10269
text:
Expecting variable name, \<variable_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The variable named in the message was not found in the netCDF boundary condition file. TUFLOW FV expected this variable (typically the time variable) to be present in order to read the boundary condition data.


Suggestions
Check that the variable name configured for the boundary condition matches a variable that exists in the netCDF file. Use a tool such as the TUFLOW FV Python Toolbox or TUFLOW FV MATLAB Toolbox to inspect the variable names in the file.

title: Message 10271
text:
No variable value specified on line \<line_number\> - "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Set Variable  == command was found on the line shown in the message with a variable name but no value. The Set Variable  == command requires both a variable name and a value to be specified.


Suggestions
Update the line to use the format Set Variable  == . For example, Set Variable MY_VARIABLE == 1.0 would set the variable named MY_VARIABLE to the value 1.0.

title: Message 10273
text:
UNABLE TO DETERMINE FILE FORMAT: \<file_name\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The format of the material file named in the message could not be determined from its file extension. Material files must be .shp or .mif format.


Suggestions
Check that the material file has a .shp or .mif extension, or use the Set Mat == keyword to assign materials directly without a file.

title: Message 10275
text:
Unexpected line encountered in file: \<line_text\>, Line \<line_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unrecognised line when reading an input file. The filename and line number are reported in the message. This can occur when reading mesh files (.2dm) or triangulated irregular network (TIN) files.


Suggestions
Open the file at the line number reported and check the content. Common causes include a corrupt or truncated file, an unsupported file format version, or content that does not conform to the expected format for that file type.
If the file was exported from a meshing or GIS tool, re-export it and verify the output format is compatible with TUFLOW FV.

title: Message 10277
text:
transport file dimensions are not compatible



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The dimensions of the transport netCDF file (number of cells, faces or vertical transport interfaces) do not match the current model domain.


Suggestions
Ensure the transport file was generated from the same mesh and 3D configuration as the current simulation. If the mesh or 3D configuration has been modified since the transport file was created, a new transport file must be generated.

title: Message 10279
text:
\<column_name\> column not found in csv file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A required column header was not found when reading a csv input file. The column header that could not be matched is reported in the message. This error is raised from several csv reading routines and can occur with boundary condition files, layer definition files, culvert definition files and other csv inputs.


Suggestions
Check the csv file for the column header shown in the message. Column headers are not case-sensitive. Common causes include a typographical error in the column header or a missing column.
The error stack in the log output identifies which routine triggered the read and can help narrow down which file to check.

title: Message 10281
text:
\<event_name\> not found in Event File



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The event name shown in the message was not found in the Event File. All event names specified for the simulation must match entries defined in the Event File.


Suggestions
Check that the event name matches a Define Event == block in the Event File. Event names are case-insensitive but must otherwise match exactly.

title: Message 10283
text:
\<data_variable\> variable not found in netcdf file. Assigning a \<default_value\> value.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A variable name expected by TUFLOW FV was not found in the netCDF file being read. The variable is optional and the simulation will continue using the default value shown in the message. This warning may indicate that the variable name in the file does not exactly match the name TUFLOW FV expects.


Suggestions
Check that the variable name in the netCDF file matches the name shown in the warning. If the variable is intentionally omitted and the default value shown is appropriate for the model then the warning can be ignored. If the default value is not appropriate then add the missing variable to the netCDF file.
For models that include advection dispersion (temperature, salinity or tracers), sediment transport or water quality a default value of NaN typically means the model will use internal model concentrations at the boundary condition location.
This can be desirable and in these situations a user may deliberately use a dummy variable name to ensure the NaN default is applied.

title: Message 10285
text:
Cannot use "DEFINE EVENT" inside another "DEFINE EVENT" block. Line no: \<line_number\> : "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A Define Event block was found nested inside another Define Event block on the line shown in the message. Define Event blocks cannot be nested.


Suggestions
Close the current Define Event block with End Define before starting a new one.

title: Message 10287
text:
Number of include file nests is greater than maximum allowed, \<max_include_nests\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The maximum allowed depth of nested include files has been exceeded. Include files can reference other include files but the nesting depth cannot exceed the limit shown in the message.


Suggestions
Reduce the depth of include file nesting in the control file structure by flattening the hierarchy or consolidating content into fewer levels of include files.

title: Message 10289
text:
Unbalanced "IF"/"END IF" count. Line no: \<line_number\> : "\<line_text\>"



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An If Scenario or If Event block was opened without a matching End If. Every If Scenario or If Event must be closed with a corresponding End If.


Suggestions
Check the control file for a missing End If at or before the line shown, or an End If that has no matching If Scenario or If Event.

title: Message 10291
text:
Duplicate scenario number: \<scenario_key\> \<scenario_value_1\>, \<scenario_key\> \<scenario_value_2\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The same scenario key (for example s1) was assigned a value more than once. Each scenario position can only be assigned one value. The message shows the key and both conflicting values.


Suggestions
Check the command line arguments and control file for duplicate scenario assignments and remove the duplicate(s).

title: Message 10293
text:
Exceeded allowed maximum scenarios number (\<scenario_key\>\<max_scenarios\>~) in FVC name



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A scenario placeholder in the control file name (such as ~s3~) references a scenario number that exceeds the maximum allowed. The message shows the scenario key and the maximum permitted number.


Suggestions
Check the control file name for scenario placeholders and ensure no placeholder references a number greater than the maximum shown in the message.

title: Message 10295
text:
Missing a "~" after scenario/event placeholder in FVC name



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A scenario or event placeholder in the control file name is missing a closing ~. The end of the filename was reached before the placeholder was closed. Placeholders must follow the format ~s1~ or ~e1~, with both an opening and closing ~.


Suggestions
Check the control file name for incomplete scenario or event placeholders and add the missing closing ~.

title: Message 10297
text:
Unable to parse scenario number as integer: \<scenario_number\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The scenario or event number in a placeholder in the control file name could not be read as an integer. The value shown in the message was found between the ~s or ~e prefix and the closing ~ but is not a valid number.


Suggestions
Check the control file name for scenario or event placeholders and ensure the number between the prefix and closing ~ is a valid integer (for example, ~s2~ not ~sA~).

title: Message 10299
text:
Scenario must use a number between \<scenario_lower_bound\>1 to \<scenario_upper_bound\>\<max_scenarios\>: \<scenario_key\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A scenario or event command line flag uses a number that is either not a valid integer or is outside the allowed range of 1 to the maximum shown in the message. For example, -s0 or -s99 would be invalid if the maximum is 9.


Suggestions
Check the scenario or event flags and ensure the number is a valid integer within the allowed range.

title: Message 10301
text:
A valid trigger value must be specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An operational structure control block using the trigger control type was configured without a valid Trigger Value == command.


Suggestions
Add a Trigger Value to the structure trigger configuration. If the trigger is resettable, also ensure a reset Trigger Reset value is specified.

title: Message 10303
text:
Airflow_Compressor control parameter must be used for compressor destratification unit



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A destratification unit structure using the compressor airflow option and operational control block was configured with a control parameter other than Airflow_Compressor.


Suggestions
Change the control parameter for the compressor destratification structure to Airflow_Compressor.

title: Message 10305
text:
Bubbler destratification unit is only supported with the 3D module.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A destratification unit with the bubbler airflow option was specified but the simulation is not running with the 3D module. Destratification unit structure types require a 3D simulation.


Suggestions
Enable the 3D module for the simulation, or remove the destratification unit if 3D modelling is not required.

title: Message 10307
text:
Bubbler elevation is outside water column bounds.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The elevation of the bubbler diffuser is outside the bounds of the water column at the time of the destratification calculation. The bubbler elevation must be between the bed and the water surface for the calculation to proceed.


Suggestions
Check the bubbler elevation specified for the destratification unit and ensure it is within the expected water column range. This may also occur if the water level drops below the bubbler elevation during the simulation.

title: Message 10309
text:
Cell index \<cell_id\> is invalid: exceeds cell count (\<max_cell_id\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The cell index specified for a structure zone exceeds the total number of cells in the mesh. The cell ID and the maximum valid cell index are both shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the cell ID configured for the structure zone and ensure it corresponds to a valid cell in the mesh.

title: Message 10311
text:
Control type SAMPLE does not support multiple controls yet.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sample structure control type Control == Sample was configured with more than one control parameter. Only one control parameter is currently supported with the sample control type.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of Control Parameter == input values to one, rather than a comma delimited list or multiple values.

title: Message 10313
text:
Control type TRIGGER does not support multiple controls yet.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The trigger structure control type Control == Trigger was configured with more than one control parameter. Only one control parameter is currently supported with the trigger control type.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of Control Parameter == input values to one, rather than a comma delimited list or multiple values.

title: Message 10315
text:
Crest length property has not been set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A crest length property for a wave pump structure has not been set. Both crest length properties are required for the wave pump structure type.


Suggestions
Set the crest length properties in the wave pump structure configuration.

title: Message 10317
text:
Error echoing spatial structure log file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred while writing the spatial structure log file _geo_struct.csv. This may indicate a file access or disk write issue.


Suggestions
Check that the log output directory exists and is writable and that there is sufficient disk space available.

title: Message 10319
text:
Failed mass conservation check in destratification routine.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The destratification unit’s inflow and outflow rates did not balance to within acceptable tolerance. This flow imbalance typically occurs when:

The water body is already well-mixed (and therefore no density stratification to destratify)
The specified air flow rate exceeds the unit’s design capacity
The unit intake or discharge positioning is incorrect



Suggestions
Verify the model inputs during the error timestep. Check the water temperature/density profile immediately before the error.
If the water body is already well-mixed the destratification operation may not be needed at that time. Consider switching off air flow during well-mixed periods using an operational control block.
If the water body is stratified, review the destratification unit configuration as follows. - Check the specified air flow rate and number of units. Is the total air flow rate typical for the unit’s design capacity? - Enable structure flux output reporting and review the entrained and detrained fluxes in the context of overall water body volume. Reduce the air flow rate or number of units if the fluxes are too high - Verify the structure operational elevation is correct and if the model water level has gone below the structure elevation - Review operational control settings and timing

title: Message 10321
text:
Gate opening height has not been set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not find the gate opening height for a radial gate weir structure. The Radial Gate Properties == command is required but has not been set.


Suggestions
Add Radial Gate Properties == to the structure control block. The first value must specify the gate opening height (dz above the weir crest).

title: Message 10323
text:
No polygon corresponding to ID, \<polygon_id\>, found in file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not find a polygon with the specified ID in the polygon csv file. The zone ID named in the message does not match any entry in the file.


Suggestions
Check that the zone ID in the structure definition matches an ID in the polygon csv file. IDs are case-insensitive but must otherwise match exactly. Verify the correct file is referenced using Polygon File ==.
TThe polygon csv method is deprecated. It is recommended to use the Read GIS Zone == command to assign polygons via GIS integration.

title: Message 10325
text:
Nodestring side must be specified as 'A' or 'B'.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unexpected internal state when processing a nodestring structure. An invalid side identifier was passed to the nodestring processing routine.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10327
text:
Number of control parameters exceeds \<max_control_parameters\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of control parameters specified using Control Parameter == exceeds the maximum allowed. The limit is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of entries in Control Parameter == to within the stated limit.

title: Message 10329
text:
Porous structure flowpath length has not been specified



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The flowpath length required for the porous structure flux calculation has not been set.


Suggestions
Add the flowpath length to the Properties == commnd for this structure.

title: Message 10331
text:
Radial_gate_weir_dz flux function is not applicable to linked nodestring or linked zone structures.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Flux Function == Radial_Gate_Weir_dz is only supported for single nodestring structures. It cannot be used with linked nodestring or linked zone structure types.


Suggestions
Use Radial_Gate_Weir instead of Radial_Gate_Weir_dz for this structure type, or change the structure type to a single nodestring if a relative crest offset is required.

title: Message 10333
text:
Sample point for structure is outside model domain.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Sample Point == command coordinates specified for the structure control block do not fall within any cell in the model domain.


Suggestions
Check the coordinates specified using Sample Point == and ensure they are within the active model mesh. Verify the coordinate system matches the model (geographic in decimal degress vs projected units in either meters or feet).

title: Message 10335
text:
Structure 'zone' component must be constructed.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unexpected internal state. The zone component was not available when it was required during structure initialisation.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10337
text:
Structure control logic is not recognised: \<control_logic\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The control logic type named in the message is not a recognised value.


Suggestions
Correct the value in Control Logic == to one of the supported options.

title: Message 10339
text:
Structure control parameter must be specified.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Control Parameter == is present in the structure control block but no value has been specified.


Suggestions
Provide a supported value for Control Parameter == command.

title: Message 10341
text:
TARGET_DEFICIT column must be monotonically increasing



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Target_Deficit column in the csv specified by the Control File == command is not monotonically increasing. This column must be sorted in ascending order for the rule lookup to work correctly.


Suggestions
Review the control file csv Target_Deficit column for duplicate entries or non-ascending order and rerun the model. This file format is only used for Control == Target_Rule so check that the correct control file is being used, or change the control type.

title: Message 10343
text:
Unable to read cell id



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV could not read the cell ID specified for this structure. The cell ID must be a valid integer and is specified as part of the Structure == command for CELL, CELL2D, and CELL3D structure types.


Suggestions
Check the cell ID value on the Structure == line and ensure it is a valid integer.

title: Message 10345
text:
Unknown sample parameter.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The value specified for Sample Parameter == is not a recognised sampling parameter.


Suggestions
Correct the value in the Sample Parameter == control block command to a supported option.

title: Message 10347
text:
Unrecognised flux function specification



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The flux function type specified using Flux Function == is not recognised.


Suggestions
Correct the value in Flux Function == structure block command value to a supported type.

title: Message 10349
text:
Unrecognised structure energy loss specification



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV encountered an unexpected internal state. The energy loss function type was not recognised during structure initialisation.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10351
text:
User-specified structure width is not applicable for single nodestring structure types.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A user-specified structure width was provided in Properties == but this parameter is not supported for single nodestring structure types. For single nodestring structures, the effective width is derived from the nodestring geometry.


Suggestions
Remove the user-specified width entry from Properties ==, or change the structure to a linked nodestring or linked zone type if a custom width is required.

title: Message 10353
text:
Weir crest elevation property has not been set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The weir crest elevation has not been set for this radial gate weir structure.


Suggestions
Add the weir crest elevation via the Weir Properties == (recommended) or Properties command for this structure.

title: Message 10355
text:
Weir flux function is not applicable to linked nodestring or linked zone structures.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Flux Function == Weir_dz is not supported for linked nodestring or linked zone structures. Only Flux Function == Weir is compatible with these structure types.


Suggestions
Change to Flux Function == Weir and provide the absolute weir crest elevation via the Properties == command.

title: Message 10357
text:
Zone inlet/outlet orientation must be set for linked zone structure type.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The inlet and outlet orientation angles have not been set for this linked zone structure. These angles are used for structure flux stability checks.


Suggestions
Add the Zone Inlet/Outlet Orientation == command to the structure definition and provide the inlet and outlet orientation angles.

title: Message 10359
text:
upstream water levels for structure matrix not in ascending order



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The upstream water level values in the structure matrix file are not in ascending order. TUFLOW FV requires these values to be sorted from lowest to highest.


Suggestions
Open the matrix file specified by the Flux File == command for this structure and sort the upstream water level values in ascending order.

title: Message 10361
text:
\<sample_parameter\> requires salinity, temperature and DO to be included in simulation.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Sample Parameter == DOSAT requires salinity, temperature and dissolved oxygen (water quality) to all be active in the simulation. One or more of these are not enabled for this run.


Suggestions
Ensure that salinity, temperature and at least one water quality class are all enabled in the simulation before using Sample Parameter == DOSAT.

title: Message 10363
text:
NaN returned from external turbulence module



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The external turbulence module returned a NaN (not-a-number) value for the eddy viscosity or diffusivity. This indicates an instability within the external turbulence closure during the simulation.


Suggestions
Review the turbulence model settings and check the model for numerically extreme conditions such as very large velocities or sharp gradients. Reducing the timestep via the Turbulence Update dt command may help stabilise the solution.
Consider using TUFLOW FV’s internal Vertical Mixing Model == options.

title: Message 10365
text:
Generic turbulence model parameter not set



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
Unexpected turbulence model parameter set.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10367
text:
Error in reading -pu option



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The -pu command line argument could not be parsed. This argument is used to specify the GPU Device ID and must be followed immediately by a valid integer (for example, -pu0 or -pu1).


Suggestions
Check the -pu argument passed on the command line and ensure it is immediately followed by a valid integer device ID with no spaces.

title: Message 10369
text:
Unknown option, \<command_line_argument\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised argument was passed on the command line. The unrecognised argument is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the command line arguments and remove or correct any unrecognised options.

title: Message 10371
text:
User defined second order turbulence parameters not supported yet.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
User defined second order turbulence parameters are not supported. Only the built in parameter groups are currently available.


Suggestions
Use a supported parameter group with Second Order Vertical Mixing Model Parameter Group ==.

title: Message 10373
text:
bilinear interpolation weights calculation didn't converge



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The bilinear interpolation weight calculation for a quadrilateral cell did not converge within the maximum number of iterations. The best available approximation will be used and the simulation will continue. This may indicate a highly distorted cell in the mesh.


Suggestions
Review the mesh quality for highly skewed or distorted cells. Improving mesh quality in affected areas may resolve this warning.

title: Message 10375
text:
input arguments array index not same size



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An internal array indexing routine was called with mismatched array sizes.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10377
text:
xvi and yvi must be same size



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An internal polygon containment check was called with x and y coordinate arrays of different sizes.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 10379
text:
Events specified but Event File not found



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more events were specified via the -e command line argument but no event file was found when parsing the control file.


Suggestions
Ensure the control file includes an Event File == command pointing to a valid event file, or that event definitions are included directly in the control file.

title: Message 10381
text:
\<user_defined_message\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
This error was triggered by a Pause == command in the control file. Execution was paused and then terminated with the message text shown. This command is typically used within the else section of an event or scenario logic block.


Suggestions
Take note of the user customised error message and then hit entry of the keyboard to exit the simulation.

title: Message 10383
text:
Could not read projection line in .prj file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV reads the coordinate system definition from the .prj file that accompanies a shapefile. This error is raised when the projection string in the .prj file cannot be parsed. The spatial reference of the shapefile cannot be determined.


Suggestions
Check the .prj file associated with the failing shapefile. It should contain a valid Well-Known Text (WKT) coordinate system definition. Common causes include a corrupt or empty .prj file, or a non-standard projection format not recognised by TUFLOW FV.
Check the projection string of the offending layer matches the TUFLOW FV GIS template layers generated by Write Empty GIS Files during model initialisation. See the model initialisation section of the TUFLOW FV User Manaul for further details on this process. If the projection string does not match, import a new empty layer and copy over the file content into the new empty layer.

title: Message 10385
text:
Issue setting console title. Please contact support@tuflow.com



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
TUFLOW FV was unable to set the console window title on Windows. This is a cosmetic issue only and has no effect on the simulation.


Suggestions
This warning can be safely ignored. If it occurs repeatedly, contact support@tuflow.com and provide the model log file.

title: Message 10387
text:
Number of conserved variables in restart file does not match current model configuration



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of conserved variables stored in the restart file does not match the current model configuration. This can occur if the model was modified between runs, for example by enabling or disabling scalar transport modules such as salinity, temperature, sediment, tracers or water quality consituents. Variables that exist in both configurations will be initialised from the restart file. The simulation will continue.


Suggestions
Check that the scalar transport configuration of the current run matches the run that produced the restart file. If the mismatch is intentional, this warning can be ignored. Note that any conserved variables not present in the restart file will be initialised to default values.
For safety it is recommended to regenerate the restart file from the parent simualation using the same conserved variable configuration. This avoids unexpected model initialisation issues.

title: Message 10389
text:
External GIS nodestring has failed to build successfully.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A GIS nodestring could not be built during mesh initialisation. This warning is raised for each individual failing nodestring. If any failures occur ERROR 10149 is also raised as a summary.


Suggestions
Check the GIS geometry for the failing nodestring. A common cause is a path that cannot be resolved to a sequence of cell faces. Adding additional vertices along the nodestring can help the path algorithm find a valid route through the mesh.
If the nodestring is intended for hydraulic structure assignment or flux reporting ensure the BD flag is not specified in the 2d_ns GIS layer. The BD flag is only for nodestrings that need to be projected onto the boundary of the mesh.

title: Message 10999
text:
Unexpected error encountered. Contact support@tuflow.com



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unexpected error was encountered during the simulation.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 11001
text:
Material ID \<material_id\> is not specified in control file.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A cell in the mesh has a material ID that is not defined in any Material == block in the sediment transport control file and no default material has been specified.


Suggestions
Either add a Material == block for the reported material ID in the sediment transport control file or add a Material == Default block to handle any unspecified material IDs.

title: Message 11003
text:
SED control file must first be read in order to activate module.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The sediment transport module was initialised before the sediment control file had been read. The sediment control file must be loaded before the module can be activated.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 11005
text:
floating point error returned by bed mass update



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was detected in the bed elevation change after a bed mass update. This indicates a floating point failure in the sediment transport calculations.


Suggestions
Check the model for extreme or unrealistic sediment flux values. Review the output hydraulic model bed shear stress (TAUB) and sediment transport bed shear stresses (TAUC, TAUW and TAUCW if applicable). Review the specified sediment fraction models for high or unrealistic parameterisation for the sediment type. If the sediment fraction configuration appears reasonable, reducing the sediment transport timestep (using the sediment control file Update dt == command) may help resolve the issue.

title: Message 11007
text:
floating point error returned by erosion model at cell \<2d_cell_id\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A NaN (not-a-number) value was returned by the erosion model at the reported cell. This indicates a numerical failure in the erosion calculation.


Suggestions
Check the model for extreme or unrealistic sediment flux values near the reported cell. Review the output hydraulic model bed shear stress (TAUB) and sediment transport bed shear stresses (TAUC, TAUW and TAUCW if applicable). The PICKUP or PICKUP_TOTAL map outputs may assist in assessing spurious erosion rates. Review the specified sediment fraction models for high or unrealistic parameterisation of the Erosion Model == and accompanying Erosion Parameter == command for the sediment type(s). Consider use of the Erosion Depth Limits == command to reduce the likelihood of non-physical erosion rates in areas of shallow depth.
If the sediment fraction configuration appears reasonable, reducing the sediment transport timestep (using the sediment control file Update dt == command) may help resolve the issue.

title: Message 11009
text:
incompatible number of sediment fractions in restart file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of sediment fractions stored in the restart file does not match the number configured in the current run. The restart file cannot be used to initialise the sediment bed state.


Suggestions
Ensure the number of sediment fractions is the same in both the run that produced the restart file and the current run. If the sediment configuration has changed, a new restart file must be generated or the bed must be initialised from another source.

title: Message 11011
text:
van Rijn 04 external model requires that sediment fraction particle sizes are sorted from smallest to largest



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The Van Rijn 2004 external sediment transport model requires sediment fractions to be defined in ascending order of particle size (d50). The fractions in the current configuration are not sorted from smallest to largest.


Suggestions
Reorder the sediment fraction Fraction == definitions in the sediment transport control file so that particle sizes are listed from smallest to largest d50 == values.

title: Message 11013
text:
Bed roughness model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The bed roughness model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Bed Roughness Parameters == command to the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected bed roughness model.

title: Message 11015
text:
Bedload model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A bedload transport model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Bedload Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected bedload model.

title: Message 11017
text:
Consolidation model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A consolidation model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Consolidation Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected consolidation model.

title: Message 11019
text:
Depending on group model selection sediment grain density may need to be set.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The grain (particle) density has not been set for this sediment fraction. Depending on the model selections, grain density may be required to correctly compute sediment transport rates.


Suggestions
Add the Particle Density == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file. If grain density is not required by the selected models this warning can be ignored.

title: Message 11021
text:
Deposition model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A deposition model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Deposition Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected deposition model.

title: Message 11023
text:
Incorrect sediment fraction name specification, "\<sediment_fraction_name\>".
