Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A sediment fraction name referenced by a Fraction == command in a material definition or bed layer block does not match any defined sediment fraction. The unrecognised name is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the reported fraction name against the Fraction == definitions at the top of the sediment transport control file. Ensure the name is spelled correctly and matches exactly.

title: Message 11025
text:
Number of sediment layers is greater than maximum allowed, \<max_bed_sediment_layers\>.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of bed sediment layers defined for a material exceeds the maximum allowed. The limit is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of bed layers specified via NLayer == in the material block so that it does not exceed the maximum.

title: Message 11027
text:
Settling model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A settling velocity model has been selected but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Settling Parameters == command to the sediment fraction definition in the sediment transport control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected settling model.

title: Message 12000
text:
Error constructing water quality model: \<wq_model\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error was returned by the water quality module during construction. The error message from the water quality module is shown in the message text.


Suggestions
Review the error message for details. Review the water quality log file for additional information.

title: Message 12002
text:
Error initialising interfacing between wq model and ptm.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An error occurred while initialising the interface between the water quality module and the particle tracking module. This typically indicates a configuration mismatch between the two modules.


Suggestions
Ensure that both the water quality and particle tracking configurations are compatible. If the issue cannot be resolved, contact support@tuflow.com and please provide both the TUFLOW FV log file and the water quality log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 13000
text:
PTM control file must first be read in order to activate module.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The particle tracking module was initialised before the PTM control file had been read. The PTM control file must be loaded before the module can be activated.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 13002
text:
Particle/s have been seeded outside model domain. Check coordinates in seed particle specifications.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more particles were seeded at locations outside the model domain during initialisation. Those particles have been excluded and the simulation will continue.


Suggestions
Review the seed particle coordinates in the PTM control file (set within a Seed Particles == block). Check that the seed locations fall within the mesh extent and that the coordinate system matches the model projection.

title: Message 13004
text:
Unknown output parameter type '\<output_parameter\>



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised Output Parameter == command value was specified in a particle tracking control file output block. The invalid parameter name is shown in the message.
This error relates to Lagrangian outputs specified within the particle tracking control file, not Eulerian particle concentrations (i.e. PTM_1 to PTM_N) which are output via the hydrodynamic engine .fvc output blocks.


Suggestions
Check the Output Parameters == command in the particle control file and replace the unrecognised parameter with a supported particle tracking output parameter.

title: Message 13006
text:
Unrecognised seed particle type



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised seed particle type was specified in the particle tracking control file.


Suggestions
Check the Seed Particles == command in the particle tracking control file and replace the unrecognised type with a supported seed type.

title: Message 13008
text:
Error reading input file



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
One or more errors were encountered while reading the particle control file. TUFLOW FV has stopped after reaching the maximum number of input file errors. The earlier error messages in the log will identify which lines failed to parse.


Suggestions
Review the log file for the input errors reported before this message and correct each one in the particle control file.

title: Message 13010
text:
Motility model (\<motility_model\>) parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A motility model has been selected for a particle group but its required parameters have not been fully specified. The motility model index is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Add the Motility Parameters == command to the particle group definition in the particle tracking control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected motility model.

title: Message 13012
text:
Vertical dispersion model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A vertical dispersion model has been selected for a particle group but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Vertical Dispersion Parameters == command to the particle group definition in the particle tracking control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected vertical dispersion model.

title: Message 13014
text:
Wind drift model parameters have not been properly defined.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
A wind drift model has been selected for a particle group but its required parameters have not been fully specified.


Suggestions
Add the Wind Drift Parameters == command to the particle group definition in the particle tracking control file with the correct number of parameter values for the selected wind drift model.

title: Message 13016
text:
Number of conserved variables in restart file does not match current model configuration



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The number of conserved variables (scalar components) stored in the particle restart file does not match the number configured in the current run. Variables that exist in both configurations will be initialised from the restart file. The simulation will continue.


Suggestions
Check that the NScalar == setting in the particle tracking control file matches the run that produced the restart file. Any conserved variables not present in the restart file will be initialised to default values.

title: Message 13018
text:
Total particle allocation exceeds current limit.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The total number of particles across all groups exceeds the configured maximum. The default limit is 10,000,000.


Suggestions
Reduce the number of seeded particles (refer to the Particle Seeding section of the TUFLOW FV Sediment Transport and Particle Tracking User Manual) or increase the limit using Maximum Particles == in the particle tracking control file.
Note that the maximum number of particles that can be allocated is limited by the available memory on the system. If the limit is increased, ensure that sufficient memory is available to run the simulation.

title: Message 13020
text:
Particle initialisation range is outside allocated bounds. Contact support@tuflow.com



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The particle initialisation range passed to an internal routine falls outside the allocated particle array bounds.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 3005
text:
Requested device \<device_id\> not found in available device list



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The GPU device ID specified was not found in the list of available CUDA devices. The requested device ID is shown in the message.


Suggestions
Check the device ID passed via the -pu command line argument. Run nvidia-smi in the terminal to see the list of available GPU devices and their IDs. Device IDs are zero-based so the first GPU is device 0.

title: Message 3999
text:
Internal FVC error while selecting hardware option (\<hardware_option_value\>)



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
An unrecognised return code was received from the GPU solver while selecting the hardware option. The return code is shown in the message.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: Message 90000
text:
Severity \<requested_severity\> is not allowed for message \<message_code\>. Using default severity.



Release Version: 2026.2.0



Description
The messaging infrastructure detected an attempt to raise a message with a severity that is not permitted for that message code. The default severity has been used instead.


Suggestions
This message indicates an internal consistency error that should not occur under normal conditions. Contact support@tuflow.com and please provide the model log file. This will assist in diagnosing the issue.

title: TUFLOW Messages
text:
This site contains a registry of error, warning and check messages generated by the TUFLOW products.
The list of messages is provided on the Messages page.






Important



Currently, only messages generated by TUFLOW FV are included in this registry. Messages generated by TUFLOW Classic/HPC and TUFLOW CATCH are documented on the TUFLOW Wiki.





For each TUFLOW log file message, there is a page that contains the message, any alternate forms of the message, a description and suggestions on how to resolve it.
If further information is required, please email support@tuflow.com.
Each message has a unique ID number. Each series of ID’s correspond to a specific category, as outlined in the table below.



ID Range
Category
